<header>Preface</header>

# The Author Speaks

Happy is everyone who fears the Lord and walks in His ways. Their peace is their stronghold; they are generations of the Lord who were commanded to walk in the paths of uprightness that we have learned—to judge by them, to establish them for Him, and to straighten one's desire toward His work. Indeed, a person sees their duty to themselves: to prepare their way in the world, pursuing good for their people until they reach their full maturity <note>literally "their time" or "their stage of life"</note> to fulfill their decree. For a person calculates their obligation so that when the blessing returns to its source, it returns whole, and among the righteous in the Garden of Eden, they shall be filled with life; they shall not be shamed or disgraced. Every wise-hearted person has their hands prepared—not to act foolishly like the reckless—but to act in accordance with what is written, to bring merit to the many.

For great is the deed, and practical <term>Halacha</term> <note>original: "Halacha L'Maaseh" – Jewish law as applied to actual practice</note> is the goal. One's strength rises as their hand opens, and who is greater than one who holds the key? Yet, one who lacks a guide to help them return <note>to spiritual roots</note> will find themselves wanting, even when the "returning light" <note>a kabbalistic concept of divine energy reflecting back to its source</note> begins to stir within them. Even in a time when wisdom is scattered, because in a matter where there is a hearing vision <note>a spiritual insight</note> in the place where the resting-place <note>original: "Shiloh," a reference to the biblical site of the Tabernacle, often used to mean a place of peace or the Messiah</note> is withheld, it is proper to give a hint and increase knowledge. All these factors "grew" <note>original: "G-D-L," perhaps a play on a name or an acronym</note> to help me and encouraged me to rouse myself and engage in this composition. For this has long been my inner thought, even as I established my study of the books of the <term>Tur</term> and <term>Beit Yosef</term> <note>foundational codes of Jewish law</note> and settled them in my heart: to straighten my strength and increase my joy. When I met the "Sons of the Nile" <note>likely referring to the Jewish community in Egypt</note> in every place my feet trod, they rejoiced toward me and honored me like a crown. For their desire was great to prepare enough for their places, and their longing increased like silver, and indeed it was spent. Because of them, my words were spoken in my thoughts, and the sweetness of my steps ascended. Now they have strengthened me, for they are close to me, to finish what is in my heart—to show my goodness through a sign for everything found within me, specifically the clarification of some of the laws of the <term>Rabbis</term>, which will stir grace for its lovers.

And because the merit of prayer <note>original: "Tefillah"</note> is great for every person, even in the midst of the exile, and it is the highest of all levels—it is "the ascending offering"—I decided to involve myself in its laws and to prepare a straight path for its intentions, clarifying the principles of its laws in general and in detail. And in order that I may walk in a paved path, crowned with the holiness of the Holy One, I shall not lift my feet <note>stop my efforts</note> until I have also arranged its garments and its processes: to empty out its "trained ones" <note>possibly referring to the students or the components of the ritual</note> to walk in His paths. Therefore, at this time, I am moved by a willing spirit to complete the work, and not to rely on strength alone, for the task is great in terms of wisdom, and the house of prayer has high walls.

Therefore, despite my weariness, I have found an advantage in this labor. Now, for the first part, I shall begin with the order of the blessings, and I will create a structured melody of secrets and foundations regarding the laws, which follow the written words—ordered and set for all. In this, the strength of the worker is valued: to link the path of truth, for behold, thus shall the one who follows it be blessed. With ink and pen I shall open my lips, and begin with the required blessings, in the initiation of thanks and a living soul. I have drawn it only to renew the intentions and the clarification of its details. Then his hope will be satisfied in its completion, and he will have a crown in the secret of his house, wrapped in his <term>Tallit</term> <note>prayer shawl</note> and adorned with his <term>Tefillin</term> <note>phylacteries</note> for his glory.

Behold, all this is a requested gift, added to my work on the table <note>possibly a reference to the Shulchan Aruch, the "Set Table"</note>. This is now my main focus, and upon it I have poured my words. For this is ancient and venerable, and therefore I have called its name **Matzat Shimurim** <note>original: "Unleavened Bread of Watchfulness," a play on Exodus 12:42</note>, for I have made its arrangement even more so. For a complete person must... <note>sentence breaks off</note> to reveal my knowledge to the living.

-> I have created the letters M-N-T as a sign. Furthermore, the kindnesses of the Lord are with me when I remember, for He was my helper, raising me to merits and compassion from my sorrows, both internally and externally. He also gave a hint to lower my thoughts, and He mixed the light of my soul with all my fountains. My heart was not haughty, nor were my eyes raised. Likewise, regarding the clarity of his <note>referring to himself in third person</note> writing and city; for I composed this while walking through heights and storms, from place to place and from city to city, in missions and journeys, may God protect them. Amidst the many disturbances that surrounded me on every side—while this one speaks, another comes. Moreover, I have a star here, a teacher who will be with me in the end, and she was for me a shield and a protection, the heart of my understanding for my benefit. Behold, though it is a sign of weariness from the labor of your mouth and bitterness, in a generation that does not accept authority. And I am here to confess to them, when I was involved in the upheaval of the mistaken and the erring, when I placed before you a memory in the rows <note>of the text</note>, the holy and beloved ones, the high level of the excellent and God-fearing officers: **Master Joab Jedidiah** (may his Rock and Redeemer protect him) and **Master Moses Katz** and **Master Menachem** (may his Rock and Redeemer protect him), the sons of **Roeti**, the small ones <note>a humble term for the youth or the subordinates</note>, all of them chosen, all of them beloved. May they live and be like stars, a time of life and a life of tranquility and goodness. I have gathered in a proverb a crown among your people for understanding; may my gift be accepted and close, for all intentions come <-

Intentions of the Blessings

Page 3

->**The Gate of Blessings**<-

### The Customs of the Ari, of blessed memory

Rabbi Hayyim Vital <note>original: "Ha-Rach"u" – Rabbi Hayyim Vital (1542–1620), the primary recorder of Lurianic Kabbalah.</note> of blessed memory wrote the following: It was the custom of my master <note>Referring to Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), known as the "Ari" or "Holy Lion."</note>, of blessed memory, to recite the eighteen blessings with a melody before him at night, prior to the dawn. He would arrange each and every blessing at the moment he became obligated in it <note>Meaning, performing the blessing at the exact moment of the physical action it describes (e.g., waking, dressing).</note>, as is stated in the Talmud and written by Maimonides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Maimon (1138–1204), a preeminent Sephardic legal scholar.</note> of blessed memory: "Anyone who hears a rooster crow blesses: 'Who gives the rooster understanding...'; anyone who washes his hands blesses..." and so on. He would be bowed and weeping in mourning <note>Likely referring to the "Tikkun Chatzot" or Midnight Lament for the destruction of the Temple.</note>. Afterward, he would put on the large fringed garment <term>Tallit Gadol</term> <note>A prayer shawl with ritual fringes (tzitzit) worn during morning prayers.</note> and wrap himself in it. Then he would put on <term>Tefillin</term> <note>Black leather boxes containing Torah verses, bound to the arm and head (phylacteries).</note>. Afterward, he would walk to the synagogue wrapped and crowned in tefillin and the large tallit. There he would begin from "Give thanks" <note>Hodu</note> and "The soul You gave me" <note>Elohai Neshamah</note> etc., following the order of the Binding of Isaac <note>The Akedah section of the morning service.</note>. (Rabbeinu Yonah <note>A 13th-century Spanish rabbi and moralist.</note> wrote in his commentary on the chapter "One who Sees": The reason the Sages arranged the blessings in this order in the Talmud is because a sleeping person is not free to say the blessing. Since they [the Sages] were holy, they were pure and would wash their hands and prepare themselves so they could say the blessings in cleanliness. However, we, who are unable to be so careful and sit in such cleanliness, it is not proper to say them except following the order of washing. And Rav Amram Gaon <note>9th-century leader of the Babylonian academy of Sura.</note> wrote: regarding the rule that for all commandments one blesses "prior to their performance," this applies to the blessings over commandments that are the core of the institution; at that time one must bless first. But regarding blessings of praise such as these, one can bless afterward).

### Rabbi Hayyim Vital further wrote:

All the sixteen blessings arranged from "Who gives the rooster understanding" until the end of the Blessings of the Torah, a person is obligated to bless them every day even if he did not become specifically obligated in them on that day. For example, if he did not sleep at all during the night, or if he did not remove his clothes and sleep <unclear>while naked</unclear>, or if he did not tie his shoes and such. The reason is that these blessings were established for the general custom of the world <note>Meaning they praise God for the natural order of human life, not just the specific act of the individual at that moment.</note> and not for each individual specifically. Furthermore, all of them contain hints to "Higher Matters" <note>Mystical or celestial realities.</note> and it is not proper to cancel them. Except for the blessing "Who removes sleep from my eyes," if he did not sleep at all that night; and the blessing "Who formed man" <note>Asher Yatzar - the blessing after using the bathroom.</note> if he did not need to relieve himself—he does not bless them. Also, he excludes "Who has provided me with all my needs" <note>She'asa li kol tzorki</note> on the 9th of Av and Yom Kippur, because on those days everyone is forbidden from wearing leather sandals <note>This blessing is traditionally associated with putting on shoes.</note>.

### My master, of blessed memory, also used to practice:

When he was in the synagogue and heard a person reciting the eighteen blessings... he would sit and listen and answer "Amen" after them. Even if he was in the middle of the Verses of Song <note>Pesukei D'Zimrah - a section of the prayer where interruptions are usually limited.</note>, he would pause and remain silent; even if there were many people blessing, he would still pause until he heard "Amen" after them.

### Now we shall arrange the parts of the blessings according to the Secret:

Behold, when a person wakes from his sleep, he must immediately wash his hands before touching his clothes at all. It is also forbidden to walk four cubits <note>Approximately 6-8 feet.</note> without this morning washing, as is written in the Book of the Zohar regarding the "Evil Spirit" <note>Ruacha Bisha</note> that rests upon the hands. The order of washing is: he should take the vessel in his right hand—the vessel in your right hand—and then give it to the left hand. Then you shall pour with your left hand water over your right hand. Then you shall take the vessel in your right hand and pour over your left hand. You shall do this three times until there are three washings of the right, three times alternating. Likewise, wash the left three times alternating. This is as explained in the manuscript: for there are three <term>Kelipot</term> <note>Literally "shells" or "husks"; in Kabbalah, these represent the forces of evil or impurity that conceal the divine light.</note> and a band of the Angel of Death is attached to them, mirroring the band of the Holy Angel attached to the three Patriarchs. Therefore, it is necessary to pour three times. Furthermore, the Evil Spirit that rests on the hands is of a kingly sort and insists on three times and pouring alternatingly; God forbid, it will not leave the hands [otherwise]. (In the *Ginzal* <note>Likely a reference to "Ginzei Luria" or similar collected manuscripts.</note> here, the reason is that the Shell does not pass from the hands except through the power of pouring water three times alternatingly. For it is known, as written in the book of the Priestly Blessings, we draw down the flow of blessing to man through the "Five of the Ancient One" <note>A highly technical Kabbalistic reference to the 'Arich Anpin' or the 'Long Face/Macroprosopus' aspect of the Divine.</note>).

<summary>This page details the morning rituals and mystical intentions of Rabbi Isaac Luria, focusing on the timing of blessings and the specific Kabbalistic method of washing hands to remove spiritual impurity.</summary>

<keywords>Isaac Luria, Hayyim Vital, Morning Blessings, Hand Washing, Netilat Yadayim, Kabbalah, Kelipot, Evil Spirit, Tefillin, Tallit, Sephardic Customs</keywords>

<meta>catchword: Gate</meta>

-> # Introduction <-

They come from here! And even though his strength is abundant! My offering is meager in its poverty! Is there not for you a path to his integrity? In the place of his greatness, there his humility is found! <note>A classic Rabbinic idiom (Talmud, Megillah 31a) usually referring to God's accessibility despite His infinite nature.</note> Before Him, He prepared our beginning! And a will like His righteousness! For the Lord is all, and the mouth of His wisdom. For whether one does much or does little, provided that it is established in its time! <note>A variation of the Talmudic maxim (Berakhot 17a) that the intention of the heart matters more than the quantity of the offering.</note> And its correctness stood for examination! With the power of spices they were adorned! For it was not in his nature for his own glory...
Only to grant merit to the pen of the orator <note>original: "Ha-Melitz" – a term for a poetic or eloquent advocate.</note> and for every kind and friend of the children... therefore I trusted in the branch...
His kindness... praise... my death from my dwelling... He shall support my right hand and hold...
and his child... and He shall be a shield for me... behind my steps...
and to dwell for me... and always all...
my days stood like a shadow.
Standing for their King
with a voice.

---

### Words of the Supervisor of the Printing

**M** - High world! Spare and pity the soul as if I had descended from it to my mouth; its taste is like the taste of ointment.
**Ts** - A honeycomb of words for the bitter, a sweet pleasantness for the soul, and a healing for the heart; this is the **Guarded Matzah** <term>Matzat Shemurim</term> <note>The title of the book, written by Nathan Neta Hannover (d. 1683). The title literally means "Guarded Matzah," referring to the Passover cracker, but here it serves as a mystical metaphor for preserved spiritual wisdom.</note>, pure from the shores of the spikenard-perfumed seas.
**Ch** - It was investigated for those who walk the path to improve their ways and to add them unto the three primary commandments: Rest <note>The Sabbath</note>, Ritual Fringes <note>Tzitzit</note>, and Phylacteries <note>Tefillin</note>.
**P** - Supervision and effort according to the words of our Sages of blessed memory. And when it came to me to print it, I hurried and did not delay; I ran.
**R** - I desired to do His will, for I said: a place of refuge for her strength, a rest for my hands toward her wisdom. And I am not a free man to desist from it. <note>A reference to Ethics of the Fathers (Pirkei Avot 2:16): "The day is short... and you are not a free man to desist from the work."</note>
**I** - It is right by law, for not only is the book itself important, but also the perfect scholar, the author, the honorable **Levi** <note>Referring to the author, Nathan Neta son of Moses Levi Hannover.</note>.
**M** - A stronghold for every holy matter and a proper blow. To carry a loaf before the known ones, for I recognized the taste in his book, a good melody.
**I** - May it be sweet to him here and now, even more so if both are weighed together; this one is needed, and it goes without saying that this one is also good.
**S** - His will was satisfied, and my strength is pure in the craft of printing; the scholar **Abraham Aboab** <note>A known printer active in Venice and Amsterdam in the 17th century.</note> did not act like a flock without a will for the word.
**H** - The scholar who is connected to it all, as every word is completed and every life-force, for he persisted in the work from the beginning until the end and adorned it.
**K** - As it comes, he bound it; may the Lord reward our work. Let no strength be disqualified due to lack or excess, for who can understand the rest?
**Ch** - Be strong, be strong! <note>original: "Chazak Chazak" – a traditional encouragement offered upon completing a sacred task.</note> To the God who granted me merit in this work; may He come and grant me merit to print many books without end.
**I** - May He increase the Torah and make it glorious. Amen.

<meta>This page transitions from the general liturgical order to the specific mystical intentions (Kavanot) and customs associated with the morning blessings. # The Intention of the Blessings

And the reason is because the blessings were not established for us except according to the general custom of the world, and not for each and every person individually. <note>This refers to the legal principle that one recites the morning blessings for the world's renewal even if they personally did not experience the specific benefit that night—for example, saying the blessing for "opening the eyes of the blind" even if one's own sight did not change.</note> Furthermore, all of them contain a hint to higher, celestial matters and a perpetual law for them. However, with the exception of the blessing "Who removes sleep from my eyes," which one does not say if they did not sleep at all during the night, and the blessing "Who formed man" <note>original: *Asher Yatzar* - the blessing recited after using the bathroom</note>, which one does not bless if they did not need to relieve themselves. There is also an exception for the blessing over "removing the sandal" on the day of the Fast of the Ninth of Av and on the Day of Atonement, because on those days, leather shoes are forbidden to everyone.

My master <note>referring to the Ari</note>, of blessed memory, also used to practice this: when he was in the synagogue and the Cantor <note>original: *Shatz*, an abbreviation for *Shliach Tzibbur*, the prayer leader</note> was reciting the eighteen blessings <note>referring to the morning blessings, *Birkhot HaShachar*</note> that will be listed later, he would sit and listen and answer "Amen" after them. And even if he was in the middle of the "Verses of Praise" <note>original: *Zimrah* / *Pesukei D'Zimrah*</note>, he would not refrain; rather, he would pause, remain silent, and answer. Even if the ones arranging the blessings <note>the compilers of the prayer book</note> established a certain order, he would still pause until he had answered "Amen" to their recitation. Thus far are his words.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut border with ornate floral and scroll motifs, enclosing the title text "Sha'ar Ha-Berachot" (Gate of the Blessings) in large block characters.</image-desc>

->**The Customs of the Ari, of Blessed Memory**<-

<margin>Ch.K. <note>likely an abbreviation for *Chok L'Yisrael*, a foundational study text</note>; the language of my master.</margin>
Rabbi Chaim Vital <note>original: *Ha-Ra-Chav*</note> wrote as follows:
At the aforementioned times, he was accustomed to say the eighteen blessings in his house, specifically at night before the pillar of dawn <note>the first light of day</note>. He would arrange each and every blessing at the moment he became obligated in it, as is written in the Talmud and recorded by Maimonides <note>original: *Ha-Rambam*</note>, of blessed memory: "Whenever one hears the rooster, he blesses 'Who gives the rooster understanding...'; whenever one washes his hands, he blesses," and so on. He was very meticulous about this in the morning. Afterward, during the day, he would put on the large fringed garment <term>Tzitzit</term> <note>a four-cornered garment with ritual fringes</note> and wrap himself in it. Afterward, he would don the <term>Tefillin</term> <note>phylacteries; black leather boxes containing Torah scrolls worn on the arm and head</note>. Only then would he go to the synagogue, wrapped in the fringed garment and crowned with the Tefillin. He would also begin from the prayer "My God, the soul [You placed within me is pure]" etc., which represents the secret of "uprooting" <note>a kabbalistic concept regarding the soul's return to the body</note>. (Our teacher Isaac <note>Rabbi Isaac Alfasi, the Rif</note> wrote in the chapter "The One Who Sees" in the tractate of Blessings: "We have received the blessings in the Talmud in this number. One should wash their hands cleanly before reciting them. Because the sages were holy, they were careful to wash their hands so they could say the blessings in purity. But for us, who do not have the ability or the same level of care for purity, it is not proper to say them until after the morning ritual washing." And Rav Amram Gaon, of blessed memory, wrote: "Regarding what they said that 'all commandments require a blessing prior to their performance,' this applies to blessings of practice... but for blessings of praise such as these, one can bless afterward.")

Rabbi Chaim Vital further wrote: "Regarding all the categories of blessings arranged from the morning, from 'Who gives the rooster understanding' until the end of the Blessings of the Torah: a person is obligated to bless them every day, even if he did not technically become 'obligated' in them that day—for example, if he did not sleep at all that night, or if he did not remove his belt or his clothes, or if he did not remove his shoes."

---

And now we shall arrange the entire order of blessings according to the ethical teachings. Behold, as soon as a person awakens from his sleep, he must immediately wash his hands before touching his clothing at all. It is also forbidden to walk four cubits <note>approx. 6-8 feet</note> without this morning washing, as is written in the Book of Splendor <note>The Zohar</note> regarding the "foreign god" that dwells upon the hands. The order of this washing is as follows: take the vessel in your right hand, then give the vessel to your left hand. Afterward, pour water from your left hand onto your right hand. Then return the vessel to your right hand and pour onto your left hand. You shall do this three times, so that in total, the right is washed three times in alternation, and the left is washed three times in alternation. So it is written in the Zohar, of blessed memory: that there are "husks" <term>Kelipot</term> <note>mystical shells or layers of evil/impurity</note> and a group of the "King’s daughter" <note>symbolizing holiness/the soul</note> that attaches to them, just as the holy King's daughter is connected to three garments. Therefore, it must be exactly three times. Furthermore, the evil spirit <note>original: *Ruach Ra'ah*</note> of impurity rests upon the hands; it is a "King's daughter" <note>in this context, a fallen spark</note> and it is frightened away by three times, specifically when done in alternation. If not, it does not depart from the hands. (In my humble opinion, this is the reason the husk does not pass from the hands except through the rinsing of water three times in alternation. For it is known that through the Priestly Blessing and the commandments, we draw down the flow of blessing, peace, and joy to the world.)

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic instructions found in the front matter of the book. While the previous page served as a poetic and formal introduction by the printer, this page delves into the mystical "intentions" (kavanot) behind the ritual of washing the hands before prayer and meals, drawing heavily from the Zohar and the teachings of Rabbi Isaac Luria (the Ari).</meta>

-> # The Intention of the Blessings <-

<margin>In the secret of</margin> the coarseness of <unclear>•••••</unclear> one must dry and clean their hands to receive the divine flow from the "Face of the Face" <note>original: "p"p," likely an abbreviation for 'pnei pnimiyut' or 'pnai pnim'—the innermost spiritual levels</note>. The secret of this is that [failing to] clean the hands causes poverty.
There is a teaching regarding the ritual washing of hands <term>Netilat Yadayim<gloss>literally "lifting of the hands," the Jewish ritual of pouring water over the hands for purification</term> in Tractate Sotah <note>referring to Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 4b</note>: "Heaven forbid, but anyone who treats the ritual washing of hands lightly will be uprooted from the world." This is because when one does not clean the hands that extend below, it causes the "Husks" <term>Klipot<gloss>the kabbalistic term for forces of impurity or "shells" that conceal the divine light</term> to suckle from the Assembly of Israel <note>the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people/the Shekhinah</note>. The divine flow then descends into the "External Ones," which are called the "Side of Death" <term>Sitra de-Mota<gloss>the Aramaic term for the demonic realm</term>. Therefore, the person is uprooted from the world—this is a "measure for measure" punishment.

Furthermore, it is taught in the Mishnah, Tractate Eduyot, Chapter 5: "Whoever treats the ritual washing of hands with contempt is liable for excommunication." This means that since he does not clean his hands to receive the abundance from the Higher Kindnesses <term>Chasadim<gloss>the divine attributes of benevolence and expansion</term> and to provide flow to the lower realms to nourish them, he causes a separation. Because he causes this division between the "Holy of Holies" <note>abbreviated in text</note> and the "Assembly of Israel" <note>abbreviated in text</note>, they distance him and separate him from the "Cleanliness of Kindness."

Therefore, one must be very careful, for when the hands are cleaned, they become a holy vessel so that the blessing may be sustained before it is performed. Thus it is written in the book *Ways of our Life* <note>original: "Hirshut Chayenu," likely a corruption of "Orchot Chayim"</note>: When you wash your hands, before you dry them, you should raise them upward and bless the Lord. For this reason, we bless "concerning the lifting [washing] of the hands," even though it is forbidden to mention the holiness of His Name while the hands are still dirty. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who washes their hands should speak words of prayer for their hands."

Similarly, in the Midrash on the portion of the Torah <note>original: "Ot HaParashah"</note> concerning the verse "And he shall eat his son," it says that one must raise their hands after washing. The reason for the blessing is that the person should raise their right hand over the left, and so on. Now, the reason for the raising of the hands is due to the known secret that the "Husks" <note>Klipot</note> and the "Evil Inclination" <term>Yetzer HaRa<gloss>the internal human drive toward selfishness or destruction</term> dwell upon the hands. This matter is because the "External Forces" <note>demonic entities</note> have no life except at the ends of things and at the edges of holiness, as is known. They have no power to suckle from the higher realms in holiness, but only at the lower extremities.

Therefore, the "Impure Forces" <note>Sitra Achra</note> attach themselves to the tips of the fingernails because the nail is a "hard garment" <note>a shell or protective layer</note> of the holiness. If not for this, the hands would always be pure, as mentioned in the Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 208. Indeed, the crowns that are upon the fingernails—referring to the ten fingers—are the life-force of the "Husk" <note>Klipah</note>, and it suckles from those "sparks" that are damaged and emerge from under the fingernails. Therefore, one must be careful to cut those fingernails whenever they grow beyond the fingertips. Because that is where the life of the "Husks" resides, one must take water—which is the secret of the "Eighteen" <note>referring to the numerical value of 'Chai' (Life) or the 18 measures of kindness</note>—from the "Right Side" <note>the side of Mercy</note>, which is called "Kindness" <note>Chesed</note>. Through this, the "Five Severities" <term>Gevurot<gloss>the divine attributes of judgment, restriction, and strength</term> are "sweetened." These severities are found in the fingernails of the five fingers of the right hand and the five fingers of the left hand. The forces of the "Husks" that were clinging to those five Severities...

...which are the five fingers of the fingernails as mentioned in the Yalkut, they are revealed and sweetened there by the "Five Kindnesses" <note>Chasadim</note>. For the quality of Kindness always pushes away and drives out the "Husks." After the "Husks" have been driven from there, they still have the power to stay at the tips of the fingers, which are pointed downward. From that "Judgement," they can return and suckle through the "Right Column" <note>the path of Mercy</note> and through the arms, coming out through the "Cliffs of the Fingernails," and the "Husks" will return to gather there and suckle from them.

Therefore, immediately after the washing, once the "Husks" have been removed, we must raise our hands upward and lift them to the level of the head. By lifting the hands, the "Lights" that were spreading toward the fingernails are moved and enter their proper place, returning to the "Mentalities" <term>Mochin<gloss>higher intellectual/spiritual levels of consciousness</term> from the place where they emerged. By doing this, the "Husks" are no longer able to gather there.

<margin>As it is in</margin> the Zohar <note>Ra'aya Mehemna, the 'Faithful Shepherd' section of the Zohar</note>, it is explained that after lifting the hands, it is as is known: that Wisdom and Understanding <note>Chokhmah and Binah</note> are the "Upper Hands" of the world of Atzilut <note>the highest of the four spiritual worlds</note>, because they are "Kingship" <note>Malchut</note> and the "Six Extremities" <note>Chesed through Yesod</note> to the "Long Face" <term>Arich Anpin<gloss>the highest manifestation of the Divine Will</term>. And the "Short Face" <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>the emotional/expressive aspect of God</term> and his Bride <note>the Shekhinah</note> are the "Upper Feet" of the world of Atzilut. This is why one must raise the hands toward the "Head," which are the "Father and Mother" <note>the Sephirot of Wisdom and Understanding</note> of the "Short Face." This is called the "Head" because just as in a person there is only "Wisdom" in the head, from there "Father and Mother" receive a great flow in order to give new "Mentalities" to the "Short Face" to nourish it. And so, the Vessel <note>abbreviated</note>... "Assembly of Israel" <note>Knesset Yisrael</note>, which is the "Washing" <note>Netilah</note>, whose letters also spell out "Lifting" <note>the Hebrew word 'Netilah' and 'Lifting' share roots/themes here</note>, this is the secret of the "Lifting." One must lift them to the "Head." For in the lower world, they do not receive; how then could they give to others? Therefore, the main purpose of lifting the hands is for the sake of the "Feet of Above" <note>the lower Sephirot</note> in order to give them new "Mentalities."

And then the "Creatures" <note>angels or souls</note> in the portion of *How they support* [Tractate Berakhot] page 3, side b: It was taught: "A person must wash his face, hands, and feet every day for the sake of his Creator." As it is said, "The Lord made everything for His sake" (for the sake of the glory of the Assembly of Israel). And Maimonides <note>Rambam</note> in the laws of prayer, Chapter 4, rules that this is the law, and Rashi explained that one washes the feet to receive the "Outer Ones" <note>to purify the parts of the soul that interact with the lower world</note>. Then, his body becomes pure like a priest's. However, nowadays we only wash hands for all other prayers. But from the Morning Prayer <note>Shacharit</note> until the Afternoon Prayer <note>Mincha</note>, one washes his face, hands, and feet, and after that, he shall pray.

--- Page 18 ---
<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic exposition on the mystical intentions behind hand washing, focusing on the flow of divine light through the various levels of the "divine personae" (Partzufim).</meta>

-> # The Intention of the Blessings <-

And now, through the act of washing, we awaken the thoughts of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah<gloss>the first flash of intuition or "Father" principle in the Sefirot</term> and **Understanding** <term>Binah<gloss>the intellectual processing or "Mother" principle in the Sefirot</term>, as well as the secret of the two arms—Right and Left—of the **Great Face** <term>Arich Anpin<gloss>The Macroprosopus, representing the Divine Will and the most hidden aspect of the Godhead</term>. This is because the inner garments of the soul are the two arms of the Great Face. Here, Wisdom is concealed, and the Right Arm holds the vessel in its hand, which is its **Foundation** <term>Yesod<gloss>the channel of transmission or procreation in the divine system</term>, and it pours into the Foundation of Understanding. 

This is the "droplet" that represents the Left Arm, which surrounds the "Feminine Waters" <note>original: "Mayim Nukvin"—the spiritual arousal or prayers rising from below to draw down divine grace</note>. These are the Five Kindnesses <note>Chasadim</note> which are placed upon the right hand, representing the Five Kindnesses within the Foundation of Wisdom, known as the **Right Hand**. Grace in Wisdom pours the "Masculine Waters" <note>original: "Mayim Dechurin"—the descending flow of divine light from above</note> upon the left hand, which are the Five Kindnesses within the Foundation of Understanding, which is called **Strength** <term>Gevurah<gloss>the attribute of judgment and restraint</term> relative to Wisdom, and is known as the **Left Hand**. 

When Wisdom enters into Understanding, and the "droplet" enters into the head of the **Small Face** <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>The Microprosopus, the central emotive structure of the Sefirot, often identified with the Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, the Foundation of Understanding (which is the Knowledge of the Small Face) pours from the waters of Kindness of Wisdom into the **Crown** <term>Keter<gloss>the highest point of the Small Face</term>. From the power of Wisdom and Kindness, it pours into the Strength of the Small Face, and from Understanding to the Small Face. This Strength then pours through the **Beauty** <term>Tiferet<gloss>the central balancing point of the heart</term> of the Small Face onto the "opening" of the Small Face. From the power of the Small Face, the water is poured onto the "chest" of the Small Face, for in the Small Face there are also "arms" <note>referring to the internal structure of the divine emanations</note>. 

Thus, the "leaning" of the waters is completed with precise thought. Therefore, Right and Water [correspond to] Left. 

As for the fourth pouring of water, it is intended to halt the [external forces] mentioned above. The reason is that the Light pours the water into the Foundation of the Small Face, and there the Kindnesses and the Masculine Waters stir together; this is the divine influence. From the Foundation of the Small Face, the abundance descends upon the hands. This is the reason for spreading out both palms—to receive the flow within them. This is the "Bride," the letter *Yod* from the Foundation of the **Father** <term>Abba<gloss>The persona of Wisdom</term>.

---

Regarding the blessing **"Who formed [man]"** <note>Asher Yatzar, the blessing recited after using the bathroom</note> and **"Acts Wonderfully"**: This is the secret of the Upper Holy Verse: "Open for me the gates of righteousness" (Psalm 118:19). It is a "wonder" and a source of sorrow for the external forces. As long as the expansion of Kindnesses has not reached the "Glory" <term>Hod<gloss>the eighth Sefirah, associated with the legs and the containment of light</term> during the night, the "Husk" <note>Klipa</note> does not depart. For "His signet is mud," in the secret of "my voice is turned to destruction" <note>referring to the loss of divine light to the impure realms</note>. All of this occurs while the surrounding light reaches the name *Waw-Yod-Waw* <note>a specific permutation of the divine name</note>. Then the pure water comes, and all the external forces are cast away. For the Creator opens the "Closing" <note>Ne'ilah</note>, and so it is in Wisdom.

---

And after the washing, before taking the vessel, bring your two hands up toward your shoulders. You should intend to bring the two arms together inside the body. They are the "back of the house," as mentioned in the **Zohar** (Portion *Vayitan*). These arms are called *cuello* <note>original: "קוע"לוט" in Ladino/Spanish, meaning neck or collar area</note> in the vernacular. In the **Midrash Ruth** (page 80, column 1), it is written: "A person must bring his hands in after washing with the intention of his Master, and prepare his two arms as one at the time he rests his hands." At the end of column 4, it is written: "There are 28 joints in the arm, corresponding to the Lion <note>28 is the numerical value of the Hebrew word 'Koach,' meaning Strength</note>." Likewise, in the left hand, there are 28 joints corresponding to the Lion. 

The secret of this is that the two arms, which are twice the divine name <note>Y-H-H</note>, must be brought toward the body to awaken the "Surrounding Light" <term>Or Makif<gloss>the divine light that is too intense to be internalized and instead surrounds the soul</term>. One must also spread both palms during the blessing, as if wanting to receive something within them; this is a hint toward receiving the "Beginning" and "Kindness."

---

I have written this for those who are meticulous: Why were our Sages so much stricter regarding the washing of hands than other blessings, such as the Priestly Blessing or the blessings over commandments? The reason is that the essence of this blessing is in the "Holy of Holies," and the "External Ones" <note>the demonic forces</note> should have no part in it whatsoever. Therefore, one needs the purity of intention, and should only recite it with clean hands, in holiness and purity. But for other blessings, there is some "grip" for the "Destroyers" <note>demons</note>, and therefore it is not as strict if the hands are perfectly clean. 

Regarding what the Sages said: "Anyone who **treats the washing of hands lightly**," they did not say "anyone who does not wash," but specifically "treats it lightly." As it says in the Talmud (Tractate Shabbat, chapter "With what may a woman go out"), "Anyone who treats the washing of hands lightly brings poverty upon themselves." **Rava** said: "This only applies to one who does not wash his hands at all, but if he washes them [poorly], we have no problem with it." **Rashi** explains: "He washes and is still considered impure because he used so little water that it brings him to poverty." Others say "treating it lightly" refers to one who does not lift his hands upward after washing.

It concludes with a legal and mystical warning that neglecting the proper procedure for this ritual leads to spiritual and physical poverty.</summary>

# The Intention of the Blessings
## A I
<meta>catchword: to strengthen</meta>

Open to all in the future to come, speedily in our days. And there is also a "curtain" of the **Spirit of Life** <note>original: "Ruacha d'Chayye"</note> that conceals the **Holy Ancient One** <term>Atika Kadisha<gloss>the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine Will</term> toward the "thigh of the arm," which is revealed to us in total clarity. This vitality is designated for the "days of His arm" and His mighty deeds. From this, the Spirit of Life is drawn to the "thigh" of the **Kingdom** <term>Malchut<gloss>the final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the feminine aspect of the Divine</term>, which is the prayer associated with the hand where the **Phylacteries** <term>Tefillin<gloss>ritual leather boxes containing Torah verses worn on the arm and head</term> are bound; this is called the **King Messiah**. Therefore, we currently only wash our hands up to the joint of the arm. For the arm is the secret of the verse: "The Lord has bared His holy arm" (Isaiah 52:10). At this current time, the Kingdom receives the Spirit of Life through "garments" <note>external layers of reality</note>, and the act of placing the Tefillin on the hand is to indicate the reception of the Spirit of Life through these garments. 

However, in the future to come, the garments of the Arm will be removed, and the Arm will be revealed before the eyes of all nations. Then, the Kingdom will receive the Spirit of Life in total revelation without garments, but only through the **Small Face** <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>the central emotive structure of the Divine personae, representing God's relational aspect</term>. This is the meaning of "As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders" (Micah 7:15). This means that just as in the Exodus it is written that the children of Israel went up "armed" <note>original: "Chamushim," which also hints at the number 50</note>, so in the future they will go out through the secret of the "Fifty" <note>the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. This is the "wonders" mentioned—the letter *Kaf* <note>numerical value 20</note> of "wonders" <note>original: "Ke-pelaot"</note> refers to that revealed *Kaf* in the arm of the Small Face. This is why it says "Show us wonders"—specifically "show," so that the letter *Kaf* will be revealed in total clarity. This is also hinted at in the Tractate Berakhot regarding Rabbi Eliezer, who was sitting in the study house and bared his arm, and it shone with light—which was a sign of what is to happen in the future, for "there is nothing new under the sun" (Ecclesiastes 1:9).

<margin>Law 2</margin>
> When he dries his hands, let him say: "Blessed [art Thou...] who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us regarding the washing of hands."

And briefly: before the washing, one must intend to awaken and separate the **Husks** <term>Kelipot<gloss>the "shells" or "shards" of impurity that conceal divine light</term> from the external aspect of the three "shortcomings" of **Action** <term>Asiyah<gloss>the lowest of the four spiritual worlds, our physical reality</term> and to prepare their inner light. Through the blessing, one prepares their "Surrounding Light" <note>original: "Or HaMakif"—divine light that is too intense to be internalized and thus surrounds the soul</note> of the external aspects. Afterward, when you take the vessel of water in your hand to wash with them, intend that in the water <note>Hebrew: "Mayim"</note> there are three letters representing the name of **God** <term>Elohim</term>. Intend that in the "filling" of the hands there is the numerical value of the "Backwards" names of **72, 63, 45, and 52** <note>these are the four primary expansions of the four-letter Name of God, totaling different numerical values</note>. 

During the washing itself, intend in the three pourings on the right hand the **Name of 42** <term>Shem Mem-Bet<gloss>a mystical name of God containing 42 letters</gloss></term> associated with the expansion of "Yod." Specifically: in the first pouring, intend the "filling of the filling" which contains 28 letters. In the second pouring, intend the "filling" itself (10 letters). In the third pouring, intend the four simple letters of the Name. Do the same for the three pourings of the left hand with the Name of 42 associated with the expansion of "Sag." 

Afterward, when joining the two hands together, intend the Name of 42 that combines the "Aleph" expansions. Then, raise your hands upward toward the head in total devotion and recite the blessing. During the blessing, intend that the blessing itself is "Blessed to the Ancient One." Our masters said there are 12 words in the blessing, corresponding to the **12 Attributes of Mercy** of the Ancient One. 

Afterward, intend the first letters of "Regarding the Washing of Hands" <note>original: "Al Netilat Yadayim" (A-N-Y)</note> which equals 72, which is the Kingdom of Action that comes with the matriarch **Leah**, as she receives there in Action only the "backwards" aspect of the Name of 45 from the World of **Formation** <term>Yetzirah<gloss>the world above Action, associated with emotions and angels</term>. Therefore, intend to bring down the light from Formation into Action and to elevate Action into Formation. When raising the hands, have a third intention: the Right Hand corresponds to the first part of the Name of 45, and the Left Hand to the last part. The "Raised Hand" <note>the middle</note> corresponds to the root of the Name itself from which the branches spread. By the power of these "three hands," you elevate the letters in Action to Formation. This "Lifting" <note>Netilah</note> means the elevation and nullification of the lower world into the higher world. This is the secret of "the purple wool in its row" <note>referencing the Tabernacle</note>. And the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to give... and this is the hint of the secret of **Esther**, which is the secret of the "vessel" since the blessing of the hands has been completed.

# The Intention of the Blessings

<margin>From the words of my master, of blessed memory</margin>

One prays. And it appears to me that the washing requires four pours of water. And when you fill the vessel <term>Lotes<gloss>a type of washing vessel</gloss></term> with the "Voice of the Lord" <note>Psalm 29:3-9; the word "Voice" (Kol) equals 136 in gematria, relating to mystical fillings</note>, using the four fillings of the Name: **72, 63, 45, and 52** <term>Miluyim<gloss>Kabbalistic expansions of the name YHVH where letters are spelled out to reach specific numerical totals</gloss></term>. You shall divide the name into nine parts and one part into sixty, providing fifty measures of water and sixty measures of "drawn water" to nullify the four things that disqualify the water. This completes the secret of the "Crown" <term>Keter<gloss>the highest Sefirah</gloss></term>, for a vessel that does not hold a **quarter-measure** <term>Revi'it<gloss>a standard Talmudic liquid measure, roughly 3 to 5 ounces</gloss></term> is not considered a vessel for washing hands. From this we learn that the vessel itself must hold a quarter-measure. The three "faces" of the vessel correspond to the four times the Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHVH</note> is filled, and if it does not hold a quarter-measure, it does not possess the "invalidity of the Name" <note>a mystical state where the light cannot dwell</note>, therefore the cup is invalid.

So too the water must be a quarter-measure because it can be filled by the four expansions of the Name in its entirety, with every intention directed toward the Truth. And behold, these four expansions of the Name, along with the four letters of the name itself, have the numerical value of "In the Beginning" <note>original: "Be-reshit," 913</note>, which is the same as the "Truth" <note>original: "Emet," 441, though the text here uses complex Kabbalistic arithmetic</note> and the secret of the water which is within the 30 fillings of the Name. There is within it the "Spirit of Life" as mentioned. And to signify this, we find that the washing of their hands is from "this place" <note>the higher realms</note> and the washing of their feet is from "the outside" <note>the lower realms</note>. These correspond to the fillings of the Name: **72** (associated with Wisdom/Abba), **63** (associated with Understanding/Imma), **45** (associated with the Small Face/Zeir Anpin), and **52** (associated with the Feminine/Nukva), as is known. Therefore, the **Priests** <term>Kohanim<gloss>the descendants of Aaron who served in the Temple</gloss></term> were required to sanctify their hands and feet simultaneously. As our masters taught: how did they sanctify their hands and feet? He would place his right hand upon his right foot and his left hand upon his left foot and sanctify them.

The reason for this is so that they should not, Heaven forbid, cause a separation between "This" and "That" <note>between the upper and lower spiritual worlds</note>, and also to draw down the "Three Intellects" <term>Mohin<gloss>divine consciousness or "brains" that vitalize the spiritual personae</gloss></term> to the **Small Face** <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>the central emotive structure of the Divine</gloss></term>. And if you observe the secret of the feet, it is called "Kneeling" because they are the "swollen limbs" <note>extremities</note> as is known, hinting at the "three joints" of the legs. Every day, for the sake of his Creator—who is the Small Face and the Feminine—as it is said "all that is below," etc. The number **232** <note>the sum of the four fillings of YHVH: 72+63+45+52</note> represents the four expansions of the Name that can emerge from a single Name, and this is the secret of "becoming one." All these four expansions are "Above," so that they may be "Outside," which are the "Feet of the Long Face" <term>Arich Anpin<gloss>the Divine persona representing Mercy and Patience</gloss></term>, as mentioned, in order to make within them the four Holy Intellects: **72, 63, 45, and 52**. The general rule is that by right, every person should also wash their feet, as **Maimonides** <term>Rambam<gloss>Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon, 12th-century philosopher and codifier</gloss></term> ruled regarding kneeling for all. The reason we are not accustomed to doing so now is because during the service of the Priests, they were like a "Tree" <note>a symbol of the divine structure</note>, and they had a place to wash their hands and feet. But we are currently in the likeness of an "Old Man" <note>a state of diminished spiritual stature</note> whose feet are hidden, and the "feet of the chariot" are not revealed.

Therefore, the "good spirit" within us only allows for the washing of the "Food" <note>the hands that feed</note> which is the "Face" and the "Hands." But the aspect of the "Feet," which is the "Outside" aspect, we do not have the strength to wash, for "his feet descend unto death" <note>Proverbs 5:5; a reference to the vulnerability of the lowest levels to external forces</note>. Consequently, we do not wash our feet, which are the "Feet of the Feet," the very end of the spiritual levels. However, on **Shabbat**, when we ascend to the level of the "Head" as is known from the reception of Shabbat, just as one "washes his feet" in preparation for the Queen <note>the Shabbat Bride</note>, so too a man is obligated to wash his face, hands, and feet. As our Rabbis of blessed memory said in the chapter "With what may we light" <note>Tractate Shabbat 25b</note>: "What is the meaning of 'honoring it' [the Shabbat]? This refers to Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai, for on the eve of Shabbat a tub filled with hot water would be brought to him, and he would wash his face, hands, and feet, and wrap himself in linen and sit like an angel of the Lord of Hosts." This is the order of preparing to receive the Shabbat. And the reason we do not wash the "Legs"...

<insert>Written by Rabbi Akiva of Spain: and he shall sanctify [his hands] according to the secret of the 'Crown' <note>Keter</note> which is 72.</insert> Our Rabbis taught: "For the mundane [non-holy food], washing is up to the joint; for **Heave-offering** <term>Terumah<gloss>sanctified produce given to the Priests</gloss></term>, up to the joint." Sanctification of hands and feet in the Temple was also up to the joint. The **Tosafot** <term>Tosafot<gloss>medieval commentaries on the Talmud</gloss></term> noted there in the name of **Rabbi Avraham** that for mundane food, washing is up to the "fingertips" <note>the first joint</note>, and for Heave-offering, the "entire palm" <note>the wrist</note>. And the washing of hands for the Prayer Service <term>Amidah<gloss>the central standing prayer</gloss></term>, look there, it is the law even for those not washing for food. If so, the Master asks: why do we not wash this way in this current time? The Master of blessed memory answered that in the mystery of the "Black Stain" <note>a reference to the exile or a specific kabbalistic configuration</note> upon the "Nose" of the Small Face, there are two "nostrils," etc. And there it is explained that from the "Sweat of the Face," all the **Severities** <term>Gevurot<gloss>the divine attributes of Judgment and Restraint</gloss></term> are sweetened. And there, in the secret of that "Sweat," are the letters of the "Final Mem" <note>ם</note> which is the "Closed Mem" on the right. And the "Vav" is turned downward in the Second Script. The time of this "Sweat" is not during the "Spirit of the City" <note>regular times</note>. And behold, from the "Second Sweat" of the face of the "Friends," the letter "Vav" is turned and spreads, as is known, to the Seven [lower Sefirot], which are the aspect of the **Kingdom** <term>Malchut</term> in the mystery of the **Hand-Phylactery** <term>Tefillin shel Yad<gloss>the box worn on the arm</gloss></term>. Therefore, the "Sweat" is in the form of a "Simple Vav" <note>ו</note> to provide light. And now in the **Exile** <term>Galut<gloss>the current era of spiritual displacement</gloss></term>, it is drawn through the "Nose" of the Small Face, and from there it is drawn to the Kingdom, which is the Hand-Phylactery, but it remains "Narrow" because the "Vav" has no opening...

# The Intention of the Blessings

The purpose of action is to reveal the wisdom of the Blessed One in the "Beauty of the All" <note>A reference to the Sefirah of Tiferet, which harmonizes the divine flow</note>. Therefore, it is said that if one opens the <term>Samekh<gloss>the Hebrew letter ס, which is closed/circular</gloss></term> more than is necessary, it will lack the quality of the <term>Mem<gloss>the Hebrew letter מ, specifically the "open" version used at the start of words</gloss></term>. If it were opened too much, Heaven forbid, the "Judgments" <term>Dinim<gloss>the divine forces of restriction and law</gloss></term> in the world would be nullified, and the world itself would cease to exist, for the life-sustaining power of the world depends upon Judgment. 

Similarly, if the <term>Mem<gloss>here referring to the "closed" final Mem ם</gloss></term> were closed too much, the Judgments of the World of Action <term>Asiyah<gloss>the physical realm in Kabbalah</gloss></term> would remain without "sweetening" <note>The process of tempering harsh judgment with mercy</note>. They would grow too strong and destroy the world, and it would be impossible for this world to endure. Even the "Kingship" <term>Malchut<gloss>the lowest Sefirah, associated with the physical world</gloss></term> of the World of Action—which is known as "one hour" in the secret of the "hour that stands for him"—needs specific repairs <term>Tikkunim<gloss>mystical rectifications</gloss></term>. This is like the time of the destruction of the Holy Temple, when the "Persona" <term>Partzuf<gloss>a metaphorical "face" or configuration of divine attributes</gloss></term> of Kingship was destroyed because the "Strengths" <term>Gevurot<gloss>the powers of severity</gloss></term> overcame her, in the secret of the "Ninth of Av" <note>The day of mourning for the Temple</note>, when "He withdrew His right hand from before the enemy." If the Judgments were to overcome the Name <note>the Tetragrammaton</note>, even the Persona of Kingship would be destroyed.

This is the secret of **"Blessed are You, Lord..."** which refers to the flow called "Blessed" (*Baruch*) that spreads within the "Foundation of the Mother" <term>Yesod d'Imma<gloss>the channel of the Sefirah of Understanding</gloss></term>. It clothes itself in the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>the cluster of six emotional Sefirot</gloss></term>. Through the "Foundation" <term>Yesod</term> of the Small Face, the flow reaches the "Wisdom of Action." From there, the Wisdom of the Kingdom is revealed externally, "sweetening" and nullifying the Judgments called "vessels" in the secret of the "side of the table." This occurs in the World of Action, for that is the secret of the "Crown" <term>Keter</term>. 

This is also the secret of **"...and does wonders"** <note>a phrase from the Asher Yatzar blessing: *u-mafli la'asot*</note>. This refers to the secret of the "Supreme Wonder" <term>Pela<gloss>a term for the highest, most hidden divine will</gloss></term> which is written as the "Foundation of Wisdom" that spreads its light into the World of Action. The word **"to do"** (*la'asot*) specifically implies that He knows how to diminish the Judgments in the World of Action according to what is necessary for life—not less than needed, but exactly according to the requirement.

**"Blessed"** as mentioned above refers to the concept that through Wisdom, the Strengths (*Gevurot*) are repaired. Therefore, we find that the words of this blessing <note>Asher Yatzar</note> number **48**. The letters number **178**. The total sum equals 226 <note>the manuscript says 250, likely a gematria calculation involving the "filler" letters of divine names</note>. And this is the verse: "The envy of the Lord is better than wisdom than strength," meaning the goodness of Wisdom for the World of Action is the "Crown" from the Strength—that is, from the sweetening that sweetens the Strengths into the Foundation as needed, which is "Good" <term>Binah<gloss>Understanding</gloss></term>. 

But one must know that this "Good" does not come from the side of its own strength, but from the "Supreme Wisdom" of the World of Emanation <term>Atzilut<gloss>the highest spiritual world</gloss></term>, in the secret of the "Wonder" (*Pela*) as stated. This is the secret of: "And the wisdom of the poor man..." <note>Ecclesiastes 9:16</note>. For the "Wisdom of Action" is called "Poor" because of the "doubling of hands." This prayer was despised in his eyes <note>meaning the Judgments "despise" the lower wisdom</note> because it lacks the power to sweeten the Judgments in the World of Action on its own. Thus, his words—which are the Strengths of Action—are not heard by him unless through the Supreme Wisdom, as it is said: "Wonder, Counselor, Mighty God" <note>Isaiah 9:5</note>. He sweetens the Strengths for the World of Action according to the blessing. Understand this well.

When one wakes up, one says:

> **My God, the soul which You have placed**

This blessing corresponds to the "Mother of Action" <term>Imma d'Asiyah</term>. Therefore, it is a blessing "adjacent to its companion" <note>a legal term for blessings that follow one another without a starting "Blessed are You"</note>. For it is the "Mother" (*Binah*) with "Wisdom" (*Chokhmah*), who are called "companions that never part" and never cease their union.

# The Intention of the Blessings

To the Name <note>original: "הוי"ה" - the four-letter Name of God, Y-H-V-H</note> in its full spelling, filling the secret of the hidden... 13 words corresponding to the words found in the three verses: "He sent His word and healed them," "Before," and "Bless the Lord." And "I will wash my hands in purity," and "Your pious ones." <note>The author is drawing a numerical and thematic connection between the 13 words of the blessing’s conclusion and various biblical verses related to healing and purity</note>. 

Furthermore, it appears to me that our wisdom from the World of Action <term>Asiyah<gloss>the lowest, physical world in Kabbalah</gloss></term> is within the World of Formation <term>Yetzirah<gloss>the world of angels and emotions</gloss></term>, and it is known through Understanding <term>Binah<gloss>the third Sefirah, associated with divine intellect and the "Mother" of the lower worlds</gloss></term>. This is what is filled by the blessing of "He who forms," with a numerical value of 130 <note>The Hebrew letters of "Kof" (קוף) equal 100, and combined with other elements mentioned, relate to the numerical structure of the prayer</note>. 

The reason we elevate the World of Action into Formation is specifically because "Understanding" begins the process of raising Action through the five stages... The entire intention is to achieve the correct structure so that you can gaze upon and elevate Action through the secret of the "42-letter Name" <note>The *Shem Mem-Bet*, a powerful divine name used for mystical elevation</note> belonging to Sovereignty <term>Malchut<gloss>the lowest Sefirah, representing the physical manifest world</gloss></term>. For there is nothing in the world that can rise, Heaven forbid, except through the secret of the 42-letter Name, especially when lifting Action into Formation.

> When he exits [the bathroom], he says: "Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the Universe, who formed <note>original: *yatzar*</note> man in wisdom <note>original: *chokhmah*</note> and created <note>original: *bara*</note> in him many openings and many cavities. It is revealed and known before Your throne of glory that if one of them were opened or if one of them were closed, it would be impossible to exist even for one hour. Blessed are You, Lord, healer of all flesh and worker of wonders."

(It appears to me that in the morning, regarding the three blessings in the synagogue, one must say the word "Path" <note>Likely a reference to the "Bread of the Heart" or a specific meditative path</note> in its entirety, as explained at the end of the Laws of Blessings; see there).

This means that within the "Husks" <term>Kelipot<gloss>the shells of spiritual impurity that conceal divine light</gloss></term> the individual is born through his openings. Nevertheless, this rectifies the three lower stages of Action and the "internal" aspect. For in the World of Action, even in the "inner" part, there is a need to provide life to the Husks, because in Action, good and evil are mixed together. 

(In my humble opinion, the reason that even in the internal part of Action there is life for the Husks is that it refers to the internal aspect of their "garments," and not, Heaven forbid, the vessels or the essence of the Divine itself. Understand this well and do not err. See also the "Description of the Worlds" in the abridged writings of R. Hayyim Vital <note>original: "הרח"ו" - Rabbi Hayyim Vital (1542–1620), the primary student of the Arizal</note>, may his memory be a blessing).

Therefore, this "extinguishes" the inheritance of the Husks from the internal parts. This is the secret of the rectification you perform during your "opening" <note>a euphemism for excretion</note>. The matter is that the intention of eating is to "clarify" <term>Birur<gloss>the process of extracting sparks of holiness from physical matter</gloss></term> the good and the nourishment found in all foods, and to cast out the "Waste" <note>original: *Achar* - the "other" or impure side</note> after it has been clarified within the intestines. One who removes the difficult "Other Side" after it has been digested, clarified, and passed through the husk...

...rectifies his soul even more than he rectifies his body. You must intend for this. In the intention of the blessing, focus on the fact that it corresponds to the World of Action. Therefore, this blessing contains 45 words <note>The numerical value of the divine name *Mah* (מה), which also equals the word for "Man" (Adam)</note>, corresponding to the expansion of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) into the name *Ban* <note>Numerical value 52</note>. 

Have the intention to receive the light of the blessing to rectify the "Surrounding Light" <term>Or Makif<gloss>divine light that is too intense to be internalized and thus "surrounds" the soul</gloss></term> of the three lower aspects of Action. This involves the internal, external, and the surrounding lights. 

Meditate on the meaning of the blessing: "Who formed man in wisdom." The explanation is that the "Understanding" (*Binah*) of the World of Formation "formed" man within the World of Action through "Wisdom" (*Chokhmah*), as it is written: "You made them all with wisdom." Likewise, "And God said" refers to the work of Creation. 

Since each of the worlds (Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah) contains elements of Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge—namely, the Crown (*Keter*) is in the World of Emanation, the "Nest" is in the World of Creation, the "Six Extremities" are in the World of Formation, and Sovereignty (*Malchut*) is in the World of Action—behold, this "Man" (who is Wisdom) is a part of the three "Head" Sefirot of the World of Formation. Therefore, it says "And created in him," using the language of "Creation" (*Beriah*). It says specifically "in him," meaning within his very self, which comes from the level of Creation within Action.

As for "Openings and Cavities," these refer to the seven openings of the skull <note>The two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, and the mouth</note>. Regarding "Revealed and known before Your throne of glory," the explanation is that those seven aspects of the skull belong to the World of Emanation (*Atzilut*) which are "before the Throne," because the World of Creation (*Beriah*) is itself the "Throne." Emanation is "inside" the Throne. 

From above, their movements are revealed, acting upon the "Skull" of the Wisdom of Action to give strength to "sweeten" the "Judgments" <term>Dinim<gloss>the forces of restriction and severity</gloss></term> in the World of Action according to the need. For it is known that the existence of "Judgments" is for the benefit of the world; through them, the Supreme Emanator gives a "limit" and a "measure" to the light, so that the worlds can receive the light within a "vessel" <note>original: *Karsifna* - an Aramaic/Zoharic term for a boundary or lead weight</note> that writes the quota and the line of measure for all the Sefirot. 

Behold, the world is only rectified through "Judgments." Understand this very well. And if this is true in all worlds, it is even more so in the World of Action, where the need for Judgments is absolute. For there, the "Total Good" <note>represented by the number 280</note> consists of the "Five Severities" <term>Gevurot<gloss>the Sefirah of strength and restriction</gloss></term>... and the number of the essential revelation of Man.

# The Intention of the Blessings

->A sweet verse for prophecies • and likewise the Mind <note>original: "שכוי" (Sechvi) - heart or mind; gematria 119</note> is 119 in Gematria<-

### When he opens his eyes, let him say: Blessed is He who opens the blind

The influence <note>original: "שפע" (Shefa) - the flow of divine energy</note> flows according to the way of our Sages, of blessed memory, on the verse: "The King is bound in the tresses" <note>original: "מלך אסור ברהטים" (Song of Songs 7:6)</note>. "He has made you a choice portion," etc. This indicates a great matter: that a person must give thanks to his Creator for the goodness He has done for him. This is because just as the Supreme Influence is the opening of a person's eyes when he was sleeping—at which time he was like one who is blind, even though he is not literally blind—it is in the manner of "And the eyes of both of them were opened" <note>Genesis 3:7</note>. Thus, one must intend in his heart the secret of the Supreme Gaze <term>Hashgacha<gloss>Divine supervision or "gazing" upon the world</gloss></term> and the Supreme Observation which is drawn down from the "Filling of Yuds" to the "Filling of He's," and from there to the "Filling of Alephs," and from there to the "Filling of Shins." <note>These refer to the four Kabbalistic expansions of the four-letter Name of God (Y-H-V-H), representing different levels of the divine emanation</note>.

All of this is the secret of the attribute of "Day," for the Influence is drawn down as previously mentioned. However, at night, the attribute of "Night" is mentioned, and the Influence is drawn from the Filling of Yuds itself to the Filling of Shins. And then, when it is filled, this "Shin" becomes a "Filling of Yud." Therefore, one must keep the secret of the two latter Names, which are 52 and 45 <note>The Names *Ban* and *Mah*, representing the lower worlds and the human element</note>, just as is brought in the "Intention of the Prayer for Falling Asleep," so that they rest upon the eyes. For there are three "Yuds" called "Eyes." 

Furthermore, intend that upon the "Eyelids" is the "Filling of Alephs" <note>The Name *Mah*</note>, which are the image of the eyelids. For the letters *Kaf, Vav, Yud, Lamed, Yud, Nun* of the name *Zot* <note>original: "זאת" - "This" (feminine)</note> are the image of the eyelids. And the "Pupil" <note>original: "בת עין" (Bat Ayin)</note> is the "Filling of Shins" of the Crown of Sovereignty <term>Malchut<gloss>the lowest Sefirah, associated with the physical world and the feminine divine</gloss></term>, which he restores so that it becomes the "Filling of Yuds." 

And behold, the Names 52 and 45 clothe themselves in the secret of Judgment <term>Din<gloss>Divine rigor or justice</gloss></term>, which are the two "Eyes" that were "Blind." They are called "Blind" because the primary light of the eyes comes from the "Kindnesses" <term>Chasadim<gloss>the Sefirah of Mercy and expansion</gloss></term>. Now that the "Names" have departed from them, the two "Eyes" are left in this state, and the light of the eyes has departed from them. After they return to their original place, it is then called "Opening the Blind." As is known, the "Filling of Yuds" is a garment for the Name of 72 <note>Ab</note>, and the "Filling of Alephs" is a garment for the Name of 63 <note>Sag</note>. And behold, the "Filling of Alephs" and the "Filling of Yuds" <note>representing names 153 and 45</note> equal the numerical value of "Opens" <note>original: "פקח" (Pokeach) = 188</note>, which is a hint to the opening of the eyes of the Names 52 and 45.

One might also say, as mentioned, that through the tradition of the worlds, the Sefirah of Wisdom <term>Chochmah<gloss>the Sefirah of pure intuition and the "Father"</gloss></term> is not currently established. Every night, He also restores the eyes of the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin<gloss>the emotive Sefirot, often represented as a son or husband</gloss></term> through the secret of the "Gaze of the Eyes of the Ancient One" <term>Arich Anpin<gloss>the highest level of the divine will, the "Long Face"</gloss></term> into the eyes of the "Small Face." From the power of that gaze, a double Name is made: the Name 72 and the Influence of the "Eyes." This is why we bless on behalf of our souls: "Who opens the blind," regarding the restoration of the two eyes that were truly blind and have now been opened through the secret of that Divine Gaze.

### When he stretches and sits up, let him say: Blessed is He who releases the bound

I have given my opinion on this: as is known, every single night the "Straightness" <term>Yosher<gloss>the vertical, structured arrangement of divine light</gloss></term> returns to the secret of the "Six Extremities" <note>the six emotional Sefirot</note> alone. It is not expanded, but rather its stature is "doubled" or "shrunk." This means that the "Mochin" (intellectual lights) depart from it and return to the secret of "Three within Three" <note>a state of spiritual gestation or dormancy</note>. They are "Bound," entering into the "Extremities" until the middle of the night. After the Gaze returns to the Names 52 and 45, then the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah<gloss>the indwelling divine feminine</gloss></term>, which is the Name 63, has the power to birth new Mochin even for the Name 45, which is the "Small Face." Then, the "Bound" ones are released—which are the two Names 86 <note>Elohim</note> together with the two "Inclusions," which are the Mochin of the Small Face. This is why we bless "Who releases the bound," for it is the point of the foundation where they were bound, and now the Mochin emerge outward.

### When he stands upright, let him say: Blessed is He who straightens the bent

Behold, now the Mochin emerge outward from the Foundation <term>Yesod<gloss>the Sefirah of connection and procreation</gloss></term> of the "Mother" <term>Imma<gloss>the Sefirah of Understanding</gloss></term>. By the secret of the night, they were literally moved from their place; the Mochin were within the "Mother," "Three within Three," bent over their heads and their knees, upon their innards. Now they expand into the secret of the Ten Sefirot and stand upright in the secret of a "Partzuf" <term>Divine Persona<gloss>a full configuration of the ten Sefirot</gloss></term>. This is why we bless "Who straightens the bent," which is the Name 72, 63, 45, and 52, together with the four "Inclusions." This is the secret of "He who straightens, straightens with the Name," for these are the four Names of the Tetragrammaton of the Mochin for the "Small Face," which were straightened and expanded into the secret of "Existence" for the Small Face.

### When he dresses, let him say: Blessed is He who clothes the naked

**The Ari**, may his memory be for a blessing in the world to come: Behold, after he awakens his "Persona," he must arise to clothe it. And the secret is so that the "External Ones" <term>Chitzonim<gloss>the forces of evil or "husks" (Klipot)</gloss></term> will not be able to derive nourishment from the light of his body. For it is already known that the place where the "Husk" <term>Klipah<gloss>a shell that conceals divine light</gloss></term> stands and dwells is in the middle space between the Internal Light of the Female of the "Small Face" and her surrounding light. And behold, now there is a fear of the External Ones, lest they clothe themselves in the internal secret of the Female who is near to them. For from her Surrounding Light, they have no power to observe or to derive nourishment. And therefore...

Focus your intention on the blessing of "My God, the Soul" <note>original: "אלקי נשמה" (Elohai Neshamah)</note>. All of these are established in <term>Binah<gloss>Understanding; the third Sephirah and source of the soul's return</gloss></term>, through which we recite this blessing. This is the secret of "And to restore it to me in the time to come," meaning just as in the future all souls will return to their bodies, so too every morning when the soul ascends in the secret of "Feminine Waters," it will return above and not return to the body another time [at the end of life].
Therefore, one says: "As long as the soul is within me, I give thanks before You," which refers to the Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note> and Understanding <note>Binah</note> within me.

"Lord of all souls," for the source of souls is there in Binah.
"Blessed are You, Lord," the Name associated with the attributes of Chessed, Gevurah, and Binah that clothe themselves in the World of Formation.
"Who restores souls" through Malchut to the "External" parts until they are magnified up to the Binah of the World of Action. ### The Intention
Of the blessing: for you already know that from midnight onward, the Judgments <note>Dinim</note> are prepared in the secret of "burning and kindled," appearing as black and white in the secret of the "Moisture" that spreads after midnight throughout the entire spiritual stature and song (see there).
This is the secret of the "Voice of the Rooster" <note>original: "תרנג"ל" (Tarnagol)</note> which is Gabriel. He is the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> of Malchut, called "Gever" <note>Man/Cock</note> because of the "Severities" <note>Gevurot</note> within him.

The explanation is: "The sanctuary of the Lord" is the Foundation of Malchut. "Your hands established" refers to the Higher Aspects of Binah. She begins to have a portion of greatness through the "Sweetening of the Severities" of the Foundation within her.
That which existed before the sweetening was in the power of the Severities, in the secret of "Intoxicating Wine," for it was before acquiring the "Shin" <note>the letter representing fire/judgment</note> taken by the External Forces; therefore, it is in the power of Intoxicating Wine.
But at midnight, they are sweetened by the root of Binah and the seven acquired vessels in the Feminine of the Great Abyss, and the power of the Severities becomes the secret of "Joyous Wine." They rise in joy from the bond of sweetening to receive the Feminine Waters.
This is the intention of the blessing: "Who gives the rooster [Sechvi] understanding." This means He gives to the *Sechvi*, which is the Foundation of Malchut, and He gives *Understanding* so that there will be a sweetening of the sweetening, and that which was technical [judgmental] will be transformed.
"To distinguish between day and night," meaning He gives strength to distinguish between "Day"—which is the sweetening of the Severities in the secret of Night—and "Night"—which are the Severities without sweetening that exist before midnight. This allows the Voice to sweeten the power of the "Gever" [Man/Rooster] to distinguish and know the difference between Intoxicating Wine and Joyous Wine.
