## The Secret of Looking Constantly at the Fringes

I found in the name of the Ancients that anyone who passes his ritual fringes over his eyes when he reads the Torah portion of the "Fringes" <note>Numbers 15:37-41</note>, and whoever gazes upon them, it will lead to the "healing of the eyes," thus far their words. There is an extra phrasing in the verse which teaches: "And it shall be for you as a fringe" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>.

The secret is that the threads are certainly these holy merits, and they are for you to gaze upon. "And you shall look upon it" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>—for the word "looking" is like the language of "gazing at a star." This is why it says afterward: "And you shall see it," etc. And many wrote that one should look at the fringes all day, every hour, as it is said: "And you shall see it." And look at it according to the measure of our understanding. "And you shall see it" <note>referring to God</note>, and for "them" <note>the fringes</note> if you did not do so, these are distant as the "Glory" which is similar to the blue thread. (And according to <unclear>the logic</unclear> of the embroidery, from the fact that the fringes draw from the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note> of "Understanding" <note>Binah</note>, which is called "Joseph" as a cover in the exile of "Smallness" <note>Katnut</note>. And the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note> is called the letter *Vav*, the sign of the Holy Covenant. Therefore, anyone who looks constantly at his fringes is like one who "sees the face of the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds.") And this is the hint: whoever does not remove the fringe merits to receive the face of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>. For the Divine Presence is the crown for the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note> of "Understanding" <note>Binah</note>, which is the "Kingdom" <note>Malkhut</note> of "Understanding" <note>Binah</note>. And the inner aspect of the "Foundation" <note>Yesod</note> of "Understanding" <note>Binah</note> is the aspect of "For the Shekhinah is a mother giving birth to the sparks," like "Laban" <note>White</note> to the face of the Shekhinah, which is the inner part of the Shekhinah, and it is against the "Holy Zion." And it is also a great benefit for the soul so that sin does not come to his hand. And it is also good for achieving great perception. From the deeds of the <unclear>Rav</unclear> <note>likely Rabbi Isaac Luria</note>, throughout the day one should look at them twice, one after the other, without a break. Two times the word "Eye" <note>Ayin</note>, which equals 130, together they are like the names of God <note>Havayah</note> which sweeten the kindnesses and the judgments. ## The reason for wrapping in the Tallit before donning the Tephillin, and the reason for covering the Tephillin with the Tallit.

The intention is as follows: The phylacteries <term>Tephillin<gloss>sacred leather boxes containing Torah scrolls</gloss></term> worn on all days represent the aspect of "Internal Mentalities" <term>Moach Pnimiyut<gloss>internal spiritual intellect</gloss></term>. The "Garment of the Great" mentioned refers to more than just sparks; only a small amount remains after the "bath" <note>a metaphor for spiritual purification</note> to sustain the weakened state of the internal aspect of the worlds, rather than the external aspect of the worlds. It is known that even above, things were "twisted," meaning the Kingdoms <note>Malkhuyot</note> among them are the "External Worlds" which nourish the external "Husks" <term>Kelipot<gloss>forces of spiritual impurity</gloss></term>, and therefore they twist toward a state of lack. 

However, the prayer shawl <term>Tallit<gloss>the large prayer shawl worn over the shoulders</gloss></term> is not like the Tephillin, whose mentality is lacking in this time regarding the external worlds. Therefore, its holiness is always enduring, and its prestige never diminishes, for it originates from the "First Understanding" of the "Gestation" <term>Ibur<gloss>the earliest stage of divine emanation</gloss></term>. The essence of its growth occurs during the time of sacrifice before Him in the aspect of the worlds, for it is the secret of the "Encompassing Light" <term>Or Makif<gloss>divine light that surrounds rather than permeates</gloss></term> over the exterior of the worlds. 

What is the reason one must also cover the Tephillin with the Tallit? It is to simulate how the Tallit is the secret of the Encompassing Light that clothes and covers the Tephillin, which are the secret of the Internal Worlds in the aspect of the "Thrones." This is also the reason one must put on the Tallit before the Tephillin: because the Tallit represents the Encompassing Light of the Palace and the Throne. Afterward, one dons the Tephillin, which are internal and represent the "Mentalities of Maturation" <term>Gadlut<gloss>expanded spiritual consciousness</gloss></term>. 

Outside of the state of Maturation, it is good for the Tallit to nourish the external forces. The Large Tallit and Small Tallit belong to the aspects of "Gestation" and "Nursing" <term>Yenika<gloss>the intermediate stage of development</gloss></term>. But compared to the mentalities, there is no aspect for the Tallit; therefore, one must wear the Tallit before the Tephillin, since the Tephillin represent the secret of the time of Maturation during Gestation.

For example, we focus our intentions on the night of Passover <note>Pesach</note> that through the power of the Will, the "First Maturation" occurs for life, and the "Second Immaturity" for the month of Elul, and the "Second Maturation" of Wisdom alone. But afterward, in all [other times], the "First Immaturity" comes first. Since in the "Sanctification" <note>Kadesh</note>, the First Maturation appears, it was pleasant for Israel to also be given the commandment of Tephillin first, which are also in the secret of the Mentalities of Maturation. Afterward, they received the internal aspect of the secret of the Mentalities of Immaturity—and understand this.)

And one might ask, why does he say "Everything is *from* Heaven" and "Everything is *in the hands* of Heaven"? This is based on the knowledge that the current day corresponds to the four worlds of ABY"A. The World of Emanation is like the Crown <note>Keter</note> of the whole; the World of Creation is like Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>; the World of Formation is like the three emotive attributes <note>Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet</note> which are the "Three Hands": the Great Hand, the Strong Hand, and the High Hand. Finally, the World of Action is like the lower attributes <note>Netzach, Hod, Yesod</note>. It is known that the entire conduct of the world is through <term>Metatron<gloss>the supreme Archangel and "Prince of the Presence"</gloss></term>, who is the "garment" for the six attributes of the World of Formation. 

In that state, "Everything is in the hands of Heaven," meaning everything depends on the World of Formation, which is called "Heaven." All the world's conduct depends on these "Hands," except for the Fear of Heaven, which does not depend on those "Hands" that are the law of the Kingdom of Formation, known as the "Blue Thread" <term>Techelet<gloss>the blue-dyed wool used in ritual fringes</gloss></term>, for that is where Fear is rooted. This explains the verse: "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask..." for the level called "Israel" refers to what you receive in the World of Formation. The phrase "What does the Lord your God ask of you" refers to the masculine and feminine Divine aspects <note>Zon</note> within the World of Formation. "But to fear" <note>original: כי אם ליראה</note>—do not read *im* <note>original: אִם, "if/but"</note> with a *shuruk* vowel, but rather note that its numerical value is the same as "They shall fear" <note>original: יראו</note>, which is the Kingdom of Formation, the very name of Fear. The word *im* also implies a "diminishment," suggesting we must not allow the Kingdom of Action to be diminished of its Fear due to the "shells" <note>Sitra Achra</note>. 

Now, the text explains the "Hand" and the "Plague" based on the Zohar <note>Vayakhel, page 219</note> regarding the Secret of the Incense <term>Ketoret<gloss>the blend of eleven spices burned in the Temple</gloss></term>. In the secret of the letter *Lamed* of the Tetragrammaton, there was the Fear of the Kingdom of Action, which is essentially fearful because it is swallowed up and mixed within the "shells." How can it emerge from within them to receive nourishment until the time of the prophecy: "He will swallow up death forever" <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>? At that time, all vitality will be withdrawn from the "shells," and they will all die and be nullified. But for now, you do not have the power to elevate them except through the "Preparation of the Incense" <note>original: Pitom HaKetoret</note>, which repairs the world and connects it with the Kingdom of Formation, called the "Blue Thread."

There is a hint here: the numerical value of "Preparation of the Incense" equals "Blue Thread" <note>Techelet</note>. This acts as an atonement... <unclear>mergalan</unclear>... it is hinted that one should recite the Incense offering with great concentration. In exile, the Kingdom is like a "poor woman," for she is constantly desolate before the "External Forces." Therefore, she is called "poor" at this time so that the External Forces do not take a portion from her. Through the Incense, the world is repaired so that "strangers" <note>impure forces</note> cannot take from it. This is how death is consumed from the world—by withdrawing the vitality from the shells so they die. However, when one tries to elevate them through "External Fear," one risks bringing a plague upon the world. Therefore, one must separate from this through the "death of the plague." 

In times of plague, when the "Evil Shell" is let loose, one must be very careful. At such a time, one must engage in Torah, commandments, and prayer, crying out to God, and He will answer. This is why it is said of Sarah <note>the Matriarch</note> that she was among the "External Forces," poor and desolate... because "there was no fear of God in this place" <note>Genesis 20:11</note>. This refers to the exile of the Kingdom. The letter *Dalet* of the name Judah <note>Yehudah</note> was among the External Forces, representing the Kingdom of the Kingdom of Action. However, the letters *Heh* and *Vav* of the name *Elohim* remain within holiness, and the External Forces have no such dominion over them. Sarah was a prototype for the attributes of *Heh-Vav* when they are among the External Forces. Therefore, when Abraham went with Sarah to Abimelech, king of the Philistines <note>who represent the External Forces</note>, he was afraid they would take her and kill him. This is why he said, "The fear of God is not in this place," because the vitality had been reduced...

->### The Mystical Cloak and the Warfare of the Sabbath<-

The cloak <note>original: "Pelyon"; likely referring to a Greek-derived term for a mantle or outer garment</note> of its kind etc. and it stood to descend below its place, even though the Kingdom of Edom <note>In Kabbalah, Edom represents the realm of harsh judgments and the forces of the "Other Side."</note> did not come to wage war with the Philistines. <meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the commandment of Fringes (Tzitzit), specifically focusing on the spiritual significance of the blue thread (Techelet). It connects the laws of the Sabbath to the protection offered by the fringes against "External Forces" (demonic or impure energies) and interprets the biblical story of the Wood Gatherer through a Kabbalistic lens.</meta>

# Laws of the Fringes

->28<-

It is written in the chapter [titled] "The Partner," <note>Referring to the first chapter of Tractate Bava Batra in the Talmud.</note> our Sages of blessed memory established that the "Existing Pearls" <note>original: "Havayah Margaliot." A mystical term for divine lights or names.</note> are symbolized by the **Blue Thread** (*Techelet*). But on a weekday, when it is not [the state of] the "Existing Pearls," we take our prayer shawl; therefore, it is not proper to perform manual labor, because there is a fear of the **External Forces** <term>Chitzonim<gloss>In Kabbalah, these are "external" or "outer" shells of impurity (Klipot) that seek to draw sustenance from holy energy.</gloss></term> lest they prevail. This is especially true on **Yom Kippur** itself and during the **Intermediate Days of the Festival** (*Chol HaMoed*).

It is also established there that the "Small One" <note>original: "Ze'ira," referring to Ze'ir Anpin, the emotional attributes of the Divine.</note>—pious and mighty ones—had a fear of the External Forces. They would pray for grace because they have the power to stand on their own. Therefore, on a weekday, one who is worthy may do work. But on the **Sabbath**, which represents the Sephirah of **Kingdom** <term>Malchut<gloss>The final Sephirah, associated with the physical world and the feminine principle of the Divine.</gloss></term>, she lacks the power to sift and cling [to the higher lights] on her own. Not only does she lack the power to prevail over the External Forces, but she must be guarded from them so they do not overpower her. Therefore, one should prepare her like a vessel to receive the "Salt" <note>A metaphor for stabilizing divine light.</note> which has the power to bring the vitality of holiness into them—a power that prevails over the Kingdom and draws out the vitality from all transgressions, for there is certainly vitality there.

In the Torah, the verse calls the "profane" as "his garment." Why is the Blue Thread (*Techelet*) destined to exact punishment? Because the matter of the "End" was literally the secret of "Fear," as it is written in the Zohar, section **Shelach Lecha**, page 156. There it says: Rabbi Hiyya and Rabbi Levi were discussing the "Wood Gatherer" <note>The man who was executed for gathering wood on the Sabbath in Numbers 15.</note> on the Sabbath day. The word "Profane" (*Chul*) implies "Strength" (*Koach*). He was gathering specifically on the "Window" <note>Likely a mystical portal or vulnerability.</note> of the forces.

---

The Torah placed the section of the **Fringes** (*Tzitzit*) adjacent to the **Wood Gatherer** to tell you that the appearance of the Blue Thread (*Techelet*) ensures they do not desecrate the Sabbath. See to it that the External Forces do not enter the "void of holiness," for the Blue Thread is a protection against the **Harmful Spirits** (*Maziqin*).

It is known from the writings of the **Ari** <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foundational 16th-century Kabbalist.</note> that [the spiritual personifications of] **Israel and Rachel** ascend on high as a "Seal," as is known. However, **Jacob and Leah** remain below amidst the External Forces in the place of "Vun." <note>A technical Kabbalistic term or abbreviation for a specific spiritual location.</note> For this reason, Jacob is called "Simple" (*Tam*) in the discourse regarding the Generation of the Wilderness. The primary protection required on the Sabbath is for Jacob and Leah; therefore, one must focus one's intention (*Kavanah*) during the Sabbath breath upon Jacob and Leah.

This is understood from the verse: "And they shall make for themselves fringes throughout their generations" (*Ledorotam*). The word "For their generations" (*Ledorotam*) can be read as "For the generation of the **Simple One**" (*Dor Tam*). This refers to the "Simple" aspect of Leah and Jacob, as it is written: "And Jacob was a simple man" (*Ish Tam*). <note>Genesis 25:27.</note> He is "Simple" in rest, "Simple" from forbidden sexual relations, and "Simple" from the shedding of blood.

The intention here is the preparation of rest. The Fringes are intended to prevent the separation of Jacob from the Holy One, Blessed be He. For all week, Jacob is like one separated from the "Small Face" (*Ze'ir Anpin*). The entire "length" of Jacob begins from the chest of the Small Face and reaches until the end of its feet. This place is called the "Thigh of Jacob." This is the meaning of "For the generation of the Simple One" (*Le-Dor Tam*), for in that aspect of the Small Face, one needs the Blue Thread to guard them from the External Forces.

Jacob is "Simple" so that they do not desecrate the Sabbath. He is "Simple" from shedding blood so they do not desecrate the holy. He is "Simple" from forbidden sexual relations so they do not desecrate the "Foundation" (*Yesod*), for there is the source of sexual immorality. Therefore, the main intention of the Fringes on the Sabbath involves the pearls that ascend as the Blue Thread (*Techelet*).

These are the Fringes of Jacob. It is also mentioned in the Zohar, section Shelach, page 152: "When a man puts on the Fringes, he should do so every day." The Blue Thread is called **Techelet** because it "consumes" (*Mekaleh*) all the External Forces, as is known. Its numerical value <term>Gematria<gloss>Hebrew numerology.</gloss></term> is 39, like the "Dew" (*Tal*), which is the strength of the 36 forces. The name itself <note>referring to a specific divine name or the word Techelet</note> equals 728, which corresponds to the "10 Pearls" of the Sabbath.

# Laws of the Ritual Fringes

And it is known that one must prepare a part of it so that the radiance of the **Blue** <term>Techelet<gloss>The biblical blue dye derived from the Chilazon sea creature, used in the fringes. Its source was lost for centuries, leading to the practice of wearing only white strings.</gloss></term> can ascend. It was our sins that caused the [spiritual] cloaks to be taken from us; they overpowered us and did with you as they pleased. For when the "Consumption" and the "Wine of Renewal"—which is the **Blue**—is taken from them, it is called a **double-edged sword** <note>original: "cherev pipiyot." A reference to the spiritual power of the Blue thread to execute judgment and protection.</note>... [even though] in our current custom the nations of the world prevent us from having the physical blue dye, nevertheless, the essence of the **Higher Blue** reveals itself within these **White Fringes**. They are the vessels that channel the radiance of the **Higher Blue** upon him, which serves as a spiritual weapon. Through them, one has the power to subdue the **Evil Inclination**, as it is said: "And you shall not wander [after your hearts]" through the power of the Blue, as explained in the story of the **Yenuka** <note>The "Yenuka" (the Child) is a famous wondrous figure in the Zohar who reveals deep mystical secrets about the fringes.</note> and so on.

There is another hint in the secret of **Techelet** (Blue), which represents the completion (*Takh’lit*) of the Torah for those who study it, as it is written: "And you shall remember all the commandments of the Lord." It should never depart from your eyes... in the secret of the "Whole," which resembles the Blue. And a third secret is that the Blue serves as the "Goal" (*Takh’lit*) which must always be before the eyes of the mind. By wearing the fringes, one merits to always behold the face of the **Divine Presence** (*Shekhinah*).

->Whether it is permitted to enter the bathroom while wearing the fringes:<-

All commandments whose root is drawn from the secret of the Holy... are part of the secret of the **Inner Sanctity**. The holiness of those commandments rests upon them permanently and never departs. Therefore, one must guard that commandment in purity and holiness from every unclean thing in the world, so that the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra<gloss>Literally "the other side," referring to the forces of impurity or evil in Kabbalistic thought.</gloss></term> does not latch onto that commandment. This applies to things like the **Tefillin** <note>Phylacteries worn during prayer.</note>, **Mezuzah**, and the **Torah Scroll**, which must be guarded from all forms of filth. 

However, all commandments that are not rooted in the **Inner Light** but rather in the **Surrounding Light** <term>Or HaMakif<gloss>A type of divine energy that is too powerful to be internalized and instead "surrounds" the person or object.</gloss></term>—such as the **Large Tallit** (prayer shawl) and the **Small Tallit** (the fringed garment worn under daily clothes)—even though their root is very great and significant... nevertheless, their essence does not permanently reside in the object. It only rests there during the actual performance of the commandment. Therefore, [after the specific act of prayer], it is not strictly necessary to guard them from impurity or filthy places. Consequently, it is permitted to enter the bathroom while wearing the **Small Tallit** and...

...to sleep in it in bed as mentioned above. For when a person enters such a place, all the [divine] radiance departs and ascends from the fringes, and the **Small Tallit** remains on him as a mere garment. 

Regarding the **Radiant Light** that departs from it: it becomes **Angels**, as it is known that from every commandment a person performs, he draws a great light from the root of that commandment. After that radiance departs from him, it becomes angels that guard the person from every evil thing. Therefore, when a person enters the bathroom, those angels created from the holiness of the fringes depart from him and wait for him outside until he exits. 

This is why the Sages taught in Tractate **Berakhot** (Chapter "HaRo'eh"): "When entering a bathroom, one says: 'Be honored, you honored ones...'" <note>original: "Hitchabdu Mechubadim." An ancient prayer addressed to the guardian angels, asking them to wait while the person attends to their physical needs.</note>. **Rashi** explains that these are the angels that accompany a person, for it is written: "For He will give His angels charge over you." Therefore, one must be careful every time they enter the bathroom to say "Be honored..." and this is actually the opposite of what Rabbi Luria wrote regarding their honor at all times. For it is good to be stringent in order to remove the spirit of impurity and evil thoughts, so that his heart will always be open to the words of Torah to study them in holiness and purity. 

One who constantly gazes at the fringes causes the **Surrounding Light** to remain upon the fringes all day through his gazing. Therefore, such a person must be even more careful to say "Be honored" as mentioned, because of the Surrounding Light of the fringes that rests upon him constantly... and likewise for one who is an expert in his craft and who always wears **Tefillin** on his arm. (Tractate Menachot, page 37).

# Laws of Tefillin

One must focus their intention, for if the physical act is even slightly mixed with unworthy thoughts or touch—God forbid—it is problematic, as all the words are spiritually linked to one another like the "known darkness" <note>This likely refers to the "Cloud and Thick Darkness" surrounding the Divine, or the concept that a lack of intention brings a shadow over the holy work.</note>. 
It is permitted to write the Divine Name upon a place that has been scraped or erased <note>Usually, erasing the Name of God is forbidden; here the text discusses the legality of writing the Name over a spot where a previous error was corrected.</note>, and the nature of such errors is well-explained.

**One must** write according to the Kabbalistic tradition <term>Kabbalah<gloss>The Jewish mystical tradition</gloss></term> with fourteen lines for each and every section. This is like the movement of thirty lines; if one deviates, it is invalid. However, in all other common practices, one must be careful to avoid invalidity. Yet the correct way, specifically according to the "Sages of Truth" <note>The Kabbalists</note>, is that there should be seven rows, corresponding to the fourteen "Crowns" arranged before us; therefore, if one deviates, it is invalid, as we shall explain in the laws of Tefillin.

**One must** leave a blank space at the beginning and at the end. Also, leave the width of a small letter between every word, and the width of a line between every line. Between every letter, leave the width of a hair. Similarly, leave a space between every verse.

**One must** be careful not to write three letters outside the ruled line; however, if he wrote them, it is not invalid. I have included this: one should not write letters that form a single word outside the margin. All letters must remain within the line and not protrude outward at all.

**One must** know that in every place you find in your signs <note>original: "Simanim," referring to mnemonic devices for scribes</note>, it is said that one must end with two "building" letters <note>Structural letters that complete a line</note> for a single word. Some say eight letters, more or less. Open your eyes and see if the letters they arranged for him were filled exactly. You should not prepare them from the name of those who include the wide flourishes <term>Tagin<gloss>Ornamental "crowns" or calligraphic strokes added to the tops of certain Hebrew letters</gloss></term> as the mnemonic **CHeLAL-NiSH** <note>original: ככללני"ש</note> suggests, which appear upon them, except for the letters that must precede the crowns, which are from the mnemonic **TTag’NaZ GaZ** <note>original: טעטנ"ז ג"ץ. These are the seven letters (Tet, Ayin, Nun, Zayin, Gimmel, Tzadi) that require three "crowns" according to Jewish law.</note>. This is sufficient for you.

->**Letters**<-
->The letters of **TTag’NaZ GaZ** are best written as simple letters and also<-
->bent, according to the rule of the crowned letters.<-

The curvature of the letter **Lamed** (ל) must be written with precision. The scribe's craft or the external measurements are of a general standard. It is proper to make them all as much as possible according to the recognized letter forms. If he did not make the "crowns," or if he added or subtracted from them, it is not invalid. However, it is best to make them all and to be aware of all opinions as much as possible to satisfy all requirements, as will be arranged before you—and may it be with God’s help.

---

Focus your intention on the entire core of the "Rectification" <term>Tiqqun<gloss>A mystical act of repair or completion</gloss></term> involved in the work of all the crowns, according to what was asked. One must focus with every single crown that you write upon the "Name of Thought" <note>original: "Shem HaMachshavah." A mystical term for the Divine Intellect or the Sephirah of Binah.</note> which ascends into Understanding (*Binah*). One can then reach the end of the "Third Taste" and the "Good End," to focus the Tefillin away from all evil thoughts and to destroy the "Ends of the Hands" through his words.

The letter **Chet** (ח): Each *Chet* must be "crowned" like the shape of two of the letter *Zayin* with a roof and "hairs" <note>The letter Chet is traditionally formed by two Zayins joined by a bridge; Kabbalistic scribes often add thin strokes called "hairs" to the top.</note>.

**One must** make the first two sections ("Sanctify to Me" and "And it shall be when the Lord brings you") with a blank space of nine letters, which is enough for three words of three letters each. Likewise, the beginning of the section must be at the start of the top line. Similarly, at the end of the section "And it shall be..." there should be a space of nine letters as mentioned. Afterward, you shall write the section of "Shema" at the head of the line, for they are "Open Sections" <term>Petucha<gloss>A paragraph in a Torah scroll or Tefillin that begins on a new line, signaling a major thematic break.</gloss></term> in the Torah. If he deviates, it is invalid. However, after the section of "Shema," one does not leave a blank space at all. If one does leave a space, it must be less than the space required to write nine letters. The three first sections are "Open" according to both Rashi and Maimonides <note>original: "Resh" (Rashi) and "Ha-Rambam" (Maimonides). These are the two primary authorities on the layout of these texts.</note>. (The section "And it shall be if you listen" is placed in the middle of the top line, leaving a space before it enough to write nine letters. In this way, the last section is considered "Closed" <term>Setuma<gloss>A "closed" paragraph that begins on the same line as the previous one after a specific gap, signaling a minor thematic break.</gloss></term>.)

According to Maimonides, this order is clearly explained in the verses. However, according to the custom of the **Ashkenazim**, even the section of "And it shall be" <note>The second paragraph of the Shema</note> is treated like the great sections, and they leave a blank space of nine letters at the end of the "Shema" section. **The Tefillin of the Ashkenazim are invalid according to the opinion of Maimonides.** Regarding these laws, I have more strength to write for myself; I would follow the opinion of Maimonides from the start, for this Torah is a fortress against all evils.

**And our Rabbi Bahya** <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish commentator</note> of blessed memory wrote: every section that is "Closed" hints at the greatness of its hidden mysteries and secrets. This is a deep secret, and "sufficient for the wise." The section "And it shall be if you listen" is "Closed" and begins after a nine-letter width in the middle of the line to reflect the attribute of "Severe Judgment," which is the "Attribute of Power" (*Gevurah*), also called the "Fear of Isaac." It is deep, deep; we desire to cover it so that it is not revealed. Therefore, it is written "and he contended with him" <note>A reference to the struggle with the internal or external forces of judgment</note>—meaning, due to the magnitude of its depths and secrets, it was not permitted to appear or pass through, for from there Judgment goes out into the world. It begins after nine letters.

# Laws of Tefillin

<image-desc>A decorative rectangular woodcut border with intricate floral and foliate scrolls. Inside the frame, the title "Gate of Tefillin" is written in large, bold square Hebrew script.</image-desc>

->(The Secret of the Laws of Writing)<-

### At the Beginning
The scribe <term>Sofer<gloss>A ritual scribe trained to write sacred texts</gloss></term> must fix his eyes upon the skins in advance. It is good to declare verbally at the start of the tanning process that he is processing them "for the sake of Tefillin" or "for the sake of a Torah Scroll" <note>original: "לשם ס"ת"</note>. Once he has declared this with his lips, the garment of holiness rests upon the skin. Then, no "stranger" <note>meaning a person or thought not sanctified for this purpose</note> should approach it, for it is holy.

The straps must also be processed specifically "for their sake" <note>with the specific intent of using them for a commandment</note>, just like the Tefillin themselves, for they also resemble ancient matters. It is also better, more honorable, and fitting to prepare the Tefillin upon skin that is "clean" <note>unblemished or specifically prepared</note>, so that no sin has been associated with it.

### Explanation
From what material should the quill be made? Know that it must be made from reeds and not from a feather. This is the custom of the Sephardim <note>Jews of Spanish, Middle Eastern, or North African descent</note>, who write specifically with a reed and not a feather. 

There is a mystical hint for this: the final letters of the four passages of the Tefillin have a numerical value <term>Gematria<gloss>A system where Hebrew letters represent numbers</gloss></term> of 325, which corresponds to "Wisdom" <note>original: "חכמה" (Chokhmah)</note> and 125 which corresponds to "Understanding" <note>original: "בינה" (Binah)</note>. From there, the secrets of the Torah scroll, Tefillin, and Mezuzah flow. It is known that they are drawn from the "Mind" and flow to "Life." There is another hint regarding the nine vowel points <note>original: "נקודות"</note>: *Kamatz, Patach, Tzere, Segol, Shva, Cholem, Chataph, Melaphum, Chirik*, which total the numerical value of "Female" <note>original: "נקב"</note>. With the three compound vowels <note>Chataph Segol, Chataph Patach, and Chataph Kamatz</note>, they total the power of 125.

### The Secret of Sanctifying
The Quill. When one takes the quill according to the law, he should focus his intention <term>Kavanah<gloss>Sacred meditative focus</gloss></term> on the name of the angel Ariel. This signifies the flow of the Supernal Light, the Clear Light from the Heights, which is pure. This represents the "Foundation of the Father" <note>A Kabbalistic term for a specific divine emanation or Sefirah</note> which is called the "Vault." He writes with the ink, which represents the letter *Yod*, the secret of the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as feminine in Kabbalah</note> who is the "Female" within the "Foundation." For the word "Quill" <note>original: "קולמוס" (Kolmos)</note> shares a numerical value with "Strangers" <note>The text here uses complex Gematria to link the physical tool to the balance of masculine and feminine divine forces</note>.

---

That is to say, the male aspect... <note>The text continues with complex numerical permutations linking the word "Quill" to the 248 worlds that depend on the "Crown of the Foundation."</note> as mentioned in the Laws of Tefillin.

### Forbidden
It is forbidden for another person to call out to the scribe until he has finished the section of writing he is working on. The scribe must read the text aloud before he writes so that he does not err and cause the Tefillin to be "hidden" <note>original: "גניזה" (Genizah); if a mistake is made in the Divine Name or certain sequences, the scroll cannot be used and must be retired</note>. This is because if he loses focus, he might write out of anger or haste. One must specifically write everything according to a model text and not from memory.

### Good to Test
It is good to test the quill before starting to write the passage to ensure there is no excess ink upon it which might ruin the writing. Likewise, before writing each and every Divine Name, one should read over everything he has already written to ensure there are no missing or extra letters or any other disqualification. If he writes the Name in a place where it is not fit to be written, it will lead to the scroll being "hidden" <note>disqualified</note> by his hand. He must be very careful, especially when pausing in the middle, that his intentions remain good, like one who serves a king with blessings.

### One Must
Before the scribe begins to write, he must focus on "The Name." He should say aloud that he must focus his soul. One who is truly spiritual will focus on each and every Divine Name... for this is the "Explicit Name" <note>The Shem HaMephorash</note> that the High Priest <note>original: "כ"ג" (Kohen Gadol)</note> would mention in the Holy Temple. This is a "Unification," and the spiritual qualities rise up to the level of the Almighty. The Name with its vowel points corresponds to six times the ten Sefirot with their inclusion. This is the secret of the union known as the letters *Vav* and *Aleph* of the Name of God <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>.

### And Also One Must
A person must be careful when writing the Divine Name not to interrupt—neither in thought, nor speech, nor action. For if he interrupts, he causes a "blemish" in the Name above and—God forbid—below, according to the mystical intentions regarding Tefillin, Scrolls, and the Cantor. Everything is tied together in the laws.

### The Writer
When writing any of the Divine Names <term>Azkarot<gloss>Mentions of the holy name of God</gloss></term> found in the Tefillin, he must do so with specific intent. Therefore, if even a King of Israel greets a scribe while he is writing the Name, the scribe must not return the greeting. Specifically, one who writes Tefillin must have mercy <note>or "womb-like focus"</note> and must not lose his focus...

# Laws of Tefillin

> And above is the Great Unity, which is <term>Binah<gloss>Understanding; the third of the ten divine emanations or Sephirot</gloss></term> within <term>Gedulah<gloss>Greatness, another name for the attribute of Mercy/Kindness</gloss></term>; its measure is <note>original: "יוד הוא ואו הי" (YOD HE VAV HE)</note>. May there be no errors in my <term>Kavanot<gloss>Mystical intentions or meditative focuses</gloss></term> nor errors in the writing, so that I am not led astray. ## Regarding the form of the letters in the writing of Tefillin, there is a slight change from what the legal decisors have written.

Tefillin for <term>Tiferet<gloss>Beauty/Harmony; the central Sephirah, often associated with the character of the Tefillin</gloss></term>. The reason is that one should never say a part is missing from the beginning. Every "stroke" <note>original: "כרת"</note> part must be in the shape of a *Yod*, as mentioned in the <term>Tikunim<gloss>Referring to the Tikunei HaZohar, a classic Kabbalistic text</gloss></term>. Its form is thus: **א**. Because the Head-Tefillin represents *Binah* <unclear>and therefore</unclear> in the changes he wrote, its form is a *Yod*, acting as *Binah*. Every letter **א** that is like the form of a *Yod* represents <term>Chokhmah<gloss>Wisdom; the second Sephirah</gloss></term> and has no connection to the Tefillin. He wrote in <note>original: "בלע"ד" - possibly "in a foreign language" or a specific scribal shorthand</note>: according to this reasoning, one must make every stroke in the Tefillin like a *Yod*, acting as *Chokhmah*. For the Tefillin of <term>Rashi<gloss>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki, the 11th-century commentator whose tradition for Tefillin order is standard</gloss></term> are one aspect, and the Tefillin of <term>Rabbeinu Tam<gloss>Rashi's grandson, who held a different tradition for the order of the Torah passages inside the Tefillin</gloss></term> are the aspect of *Chokhmah*. (His colleague, the <term>Ram"az<gloss>Rabbi Moshe Zakuto, a famous 17th-century Kabbalist</gloss></term> of blessed memory, disagreed with him on this, and argued that the stroke must always be written in the shape of a *Yod* according to the owner of the *Rabbeinu Tam* view... and so too in the signs of the writing).

Every **form** that he writes in the Name of God <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> should be in this manner:
The first **ה** (He) shall have a very small "thorn" <note>original: "קוץ" - a calligraphic serif or point</note> extending outward at the bottom of its vertical leg, indicating what is written... and this is its form: **ה**
And every form of the **י** (Yod) shall have a body, a head, and a small thorn on the head, and this is its form: **י**
And every form of the **ל** (Lamed) shall have three thorns: one on top, one on the bottom, and one in the middle of the body, and this is its form: **ל**
And every form of the **ט** (Teth) shall have its two vertical strokes like the letter **ו** (Vav), and this is its form: **ט**
And every form of the **ע** (Ayin) shall have its two heads like the letter **י** (Yod), and this is its form: **ע**
And every form of the **צ** (Tzadi) shall be like two of the letter *Zayin*, and this is its form: **צ**

The letter **ח** (Chet): [pay] heart to this: **ח**

And I asked my teacher and rabbi regarding the secret of the [letters] *Samekh-He* found in many prayer books—many have paved a path in it regarding the shape of the writing of the letters, both among the Sephardim and the Ashkenazim. # Laws of Tefillin

The letters should be wide to show that anyone who is filled with them is filled with strength and a heart aligned with all nine <term>Attributes<gloss>Middot; the divine qualities or emanations through which God interacts with the world</gloss></term>, for this corresponds to the Great <term>Binah<gloss>Understanding; the third Sephirah, often associated with the "Upper Mother" and the source of the soul</gloss></term>. I also found in a manuscript the reason why three <term>sections<gloss>Parshiyot; the four biblical passages contained within the Tefillin</gloss></term> are "open" while the last one is "closed." Since the first three represent <term>Mercy<gloss>Chesed</gloss></term>, they are open; however, the last one represents <term>Judgment<gloss>Din</gloss></term>, and therefore it is closed. <note>In Torah scrolls, "open" (Petuchah) and "closed" (Setumah) refer to the specific spacing and indentation of paragraphs.</note>

# The Scribe’s Writing Order by the Rabbi, of Blessed Memory

One must be careful to write the Head-Tefillin first, sanctifying himself and completing the prayer entirely, and then repeat this entire order to write the Hand-Tefillin, sanctifying himself and praying. (It is written in <note>original: "בלע"ז" (in a foreign language/gloss)</note> that one should be careful, according to the <term>Author of the Mappah<gloss>Rabbi Moses Isserles (the Rema), whose "Tablecloth" (Mappah) provides Ashkenazi rulings on the Shulchan Arukh</gloss></term> who wrote in the <term>Shulchan Arukh<gloss>The Code of Jewish Law</gloss></term> section 32, that ideally one should write the Hand-Tefillin before the Head-Tefillin. This is also found in the Talmud, tractate Menachot. Similarly, the skin for the Head-Tefillin should be processed first, and afterward the skin for the Hand-Tefillin. Even though in the act of <term>laying Tefillin<gloss>The daily ritual of wearing them</gloss></term> the Hand-Tefillin comes before the Head-Tefillin—as it is written, "And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand," and afterward, "and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes"—nevertheless, regarding the *writing*, one must write the Head-Tefillin first, because in its level of holiness it is more stringent than the Hand-Tefillin.)

One must also be careful as much as possible to write all the sections, even if not on the same day, consecutively without any interruption of speech whatsoever, and certainly without any "foreign thoughts." Rather, one must focus specifically on the <term>Kavanot<gloss>Mystical intentions</gloss></term> related to the task, as the matter is absolute and serious, so that no errors occur, Heaven forbid.

If the scribe is old or ill and cannot write all four sections in one sitting, he should write the first three sections and afterward write the fourth. If even this is too difficult, he should at least write the first two sections consecutively, and afterward write the other two sections together. However, between the first and second sections, he must not interrupt in any way.

If he did write the first two sections but there was an interruption between them, he should begin by preparing to write the final two sections. Before he begins writing, he should first pass the quill with ink over the word *Vayedabber* ("And He spoke") of the first section (*Kadesh*) and over the word *Vehayah* ("And it shall be") of the second section. Only afterward should he write from the sections *Shema* and *Vehayah Im Shamoa*—at least a few words of each section. If he has already written the beginning of these two sections, he should pass the quill over the word *Vayedabber* of the first section, the word *Vehayah* of the second section, and the word *Shema* of the third section, and then write *Vehayah Im Shamoa*, etc. Through this, there will be a form of mystical connection.

## Before the Writing

Initially, one must recite the prayer "May the pleasantness [of the Lord our God be upon us...]" <note>Psalm 90:17</note> from beginning to end. Afterward, he should say "I bind myself with strength..." with great <term>Kavanah<gloss>Focused intention</gloss></term>. Then he should say three times the verse: "They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain; for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea." <note>Isaiah 11:9</note> Afterward, he should say these verses:

"The breath of my nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits... for Your servant, and let Your wrath be turned away... I hate double-minded men, but Your law I love... Let all those who serve carved images be ashamed... How precious is Your lovingkindness, O God! Therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of Your wings."

->May it be Your will, that You act for the sake of Your Great Name, *Pesah* <note>original: "פסח" - a mystical name</note>, which has the numerical value of *Tefillin*. # Laws of Tefillin

**For the word "From days"** <note>original: "מימים" (Mimayim)</note>: The "closed" letter *Mem* (ם) receives three <term>crowns<gloss>Tagin; decorative strokes added to the top of specific letters in sacred scrolls</gloss></term> according to the opinion of the <term>SMaG<gloss>Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, a 13th-century halakhic work by Rabbi Moses of Coucy</gloss></term>, and this is also the opinion of the <term>Sefer ha-Yashar<gloss>A work by Rabbenu Tam concerning scribal laws</gloss></term> and according to the <term>Ari<gloss>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foundational 16th-century Kabbalist</gloss></term>. 
**For the word "Yearly"** <note>original: "ימימה" (Yemimah)</note>: The letter *Heh* (ה) receives four crowns, as established in the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and by the *Ari*.

### The Section: "And it shall be when He brings you"

**This section** is "open" <note>Petuchah; a paragraph that begins on a new line</note> and is part of the <term>S-M-S<gloss>A mnemonic for the sequence of "open" and "closed" sections in the Tefillin</gloss></term> signs. This section's spaces should extend to the end of the line and the paragraph. 
There are specific mystical intentions for every word and the ends of words, focusing on the <term>Vowels<gloss>Nekudot</gloss></term> of the Great <term>Gematria<gloss>Numerical values of Hebrew letters used for mystical interpretation</gloss></term>, because this section represents <term>Binah<gloss>Understanding; the divine emanation associated with the "Upper Mother"</gloss></term>. One should focus on the name of the Second One and the name of the Mouth <note>kabbalistic references to divine names or emanations</note>.
**Six** verses are found in this section, corresponding to the letter *Heh* <note>The letter Heh has a value of 5, but when spelled out (Heh-Aleph), it can represent different levels of Binah</note>. This is hidden within the "Fullness of the Aleph" which is the source of *Binah*. These six verses are also connected to the secret of the "Wings of the Dove" <note>a reference to Psalm 68:14, often interpreted kabbalistically as the community of Israel or divine presence</note>. These verses together equal the numerical value of the "Holy One, Blessed be He" <note>original: קב"ה (Kadosh Baruch Hu)</note> which is 112, corresponding to the name *Ehyeh* <note>"I Will Be"</note>. Within this section, there are 125 letters of the <term>Alphabet of P-V-S<gloss>A specific mystical permutation of the Hebrew alphabet</gloss></term> arranged there. These 125 correspond to the 120 permutations of the name *Elohim* plus the five letters of the name itself, showing how *Binah* awakens from within.

### Deficient and Full Spellings
<note>Hebrew can be written "full" (Malei) with vowel-assisting letters like Vav and Yod, or "deficient" (Chaser) without them. Scribes must be exact.</note>

**"Brings you"** <note>Exodus 13:11</note> is deficient of a *Yod*. **"To your son"** is deficient of a *Vav* but full with a *Yod*. **"From an ass"** is deficient of a *Yod*. **"Firstborn"** is full with a *Vav*. **"Your son"** is full with a *Yod*. **"Tomorrow"** is deficient of a *Yod*. **"He brought us out"** is spelled full. **"And he killed"** is deficient of a *Vav*. **"Firstling"** is full with a *Vav*. **"From every"** is deficient of a *Vav*. **"Firstborn"** (the second instance) is full with a *Vav*. **"Sacrifice the firstling"** the *Vav* is full. **"For frontlets"** is deficient of two *Vavs*. **"Your eyes"** is full with two *Yods*. **"With a strong [hand]"** is deficient of a *Vav*. **"He brought us out"** is spelled full. All of these are essential; any error would invalidate the parchment.

### The Crowns for the Section "And it shall be"

**"Brings you"**: The letter *Kaf* (ך) gets three crowns, as in the correction of the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*. The letter *Bet* (ב) gets three crowns, and the letter *Dalet* (ד) gets three crowns. I found in the Tefillin of the ancient masters that the letter *Aleph* (א) of this word has five crowns.
**"And he gave"**: The *Heh* (ה) gets four crowns according to the <term>Rema<gloss>Rabbi Moses Isserles</gloss></term> and the *Sefer ha-Yashar*, but according to the *Ari*, it gets three crowns, which is also the opinion of the <term>Ba'al ha-Turim<gloss>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, author of an influential code of law</gloss></term>. Some add two crowns to the letter *Tav* (ת). 
**"Firstling"**: The letters *Pe* (פ) and *Resh* (ר) each get three crowns, which is the opinion of the *Tur*. Some make the three crowns of the *Pe* cluster toward the left side. According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, the letter *Heh* of this word gets only two crowns.
**"Firstling"** (the second instance): According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, the *Pe* here also gets two crowns and the *Tet* (ט) gets five crowns.
**"The males"**: The letters *Heh*, *Zayin*, and *Resh* each get three crowns. According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, each of these letters specifically gets three crowns.
**"Firstling"** (the third instance): According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, the *Pe* gets three crowns.
**"Your son shall ask you"**: The letters *Aleph*, *Lamed*, and *Shin* get three crowns according to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*. Some write three crowns on the letter *Yod*. I saw in the *Sefer ha-Yashar* two crowns on the *Yod* and three crowns on the "left ear" of the *Aleph*.
**"Hardened"**: The letter *Heh* gets three crowns. According to the *Tur*, <term>Rambam<gloss>Maimonides</gloss></term>, and <term>Rabbeinu Bahya<gloss>13th-century Spanish commentator</gloss></term>, the letters *Shin* and *Nun* also get three crowns. According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, the letter *Kuf* (ק) gets three crowns.
**"Pharaoh"**: There is a tradition from the **Ashkenazim** <note>original: "מהאשכנזים" (likely OCR error "מלססככיס")</note> to make the letter *Heh* of "Pharaoh" looped <note>curled or "bent" in its leg</note>, but the **Sefardim** do not follow this custom.
**"To send us"**: The letter *Chet* (ח) gets three crowns according to the *Tur*. Some say four. According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, it gets three.
**"And he killed"**: The letter *Chet* (ח) gets five crowns, but according to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, it gets three.
**"Firstling"** (the fourth instance): According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, three crowns on the *Pe* and two crowns on the letter *Heh*.
**"Womb of the males"**: I found in precise Tefillin that the letters *Mem* and *Yod* of "from the womb" <note>original: "ממרחם"</note> have three crowns on each. According to the *Sefer ha-Yashar* and the *Ari*, the letters *Chet* and *Mem* get three crowns each.

### The Section: Sanctify

**This section** <note>Exodus 13:1–10</note> corresponds to the <term>Brain of Wisdom<gloss>Moach Chochmah; the right-brain energy in Kabbalistic thought</gloss></term>, the "hinge for its lips," and it must be written as an "open" paragraph <note>Petuchah; a paragraph starting on a new line</note>, full and straight. 
**One must** focus during this section on the <term>Name of 72<gloss>The 72-letter name of God derived from Exodus 14:19–21</gloss></term> and the divine name *Ehyeh* in its "full" form <note>Milui Yodin; spelling out the letters of the name using the letter Yod as a filler</note>, which has the numerical value of 148. Furthermore, you should envision before you the "Sixty Faces" <note>mystical configurations of the Hebrew alphabet</note> in the form of the <term>Eyes and Crowns<gloss>Ayinin and Tagin</gloss></term> as described in the <term>Tikkunim<gloss>The Tikkunei haZohar, a foundational Kabbalistic text</gloss></term>, and focus on this throughout the writing of this section. The <term>Vowels<gloss>Nekudot</gloss></term> should all be the simple <term>Patach<gloss>The vowel mark for the 'ah' sound, represented by a horizontal line</gloss></term> within the sphere of Wisdom. Likewise, for the fixed letters in this section, one must focus on the "Great Disclosure" and focus on the *Patach* vowel.
**One must** also divide the <term>Name of 42<gloss>The 42-letter name of God used in creation and prayer</gloss></term> into its components <note>represented by the mnemonic N-B-Y-Ch-Tz</note>. To complete this, for every vocalization, one must focus only on the letters themselves, following the sequence N-B-Y-Ch-Tz, etc., until the completion of the 28 letters to remember the 72 letters of the Name. Likewise, for every <term>Word-Ending<gloss>Sof Pasuk</gloss></term> in the section of "Sanctify," one must focus on the *Patach* vowel. This is in addition to the general intention for the word-endings, which focuses on the letter *Yod* with a <term>Kamatz<gloss>The vowel mark for 'uh/aw'</gloss></term> vowel, the letter *Heh* with a *Patach*, the letter *Vav* with a *Kamatz*, and the letter *Heh* with a <term>Cholam<gloss>The vowel mark for 'oh'</gloss></term>. This is the general intention required when writing all the Names of the Lord <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> and the name *Ehyeh*.
**Ten verses** are found in the section of "Sanctify," corresponding to the letter *Yod* in the Brain of Wisdom to awaken it. During the writing, one should focus on the <term>Acronyms<gloss>Roshei Tevot</gloss></term> of the ten verses, which have the numerical value of
**ADIRIRON** <note>A powerful angelic name often invoked for protection or to subdue negative forces</note>. This name bestows influence upon the scribe along with the three general sections of the Name of the Lord. This is a great wonder for subduing the demoness **Lilith** and all her company. Whoever focuses on this intention during the writing of these ten verses—and the three scribal arrangements <note>the Tikkunim</note>—will be protected. When the Tefillin are opened, the Holy One, Blessed be He, subdues all the [forces of the] earth, as will be explained later in the Laws of Tefillin.
**The letters** of this section total 166. These correspond to the letters of the Names of the Lord as they are specified in this section. They also correspond to the name *Ehyeh* spelled with *Yods*, which equals 161, and with the five letters of the spelling itself, the total reaches 166. For this is the secret of the name *Ehyeh* in this section.

### Crowns of the Section

**Sanctify** (*Kadesh*): According to the statute, it should have 14 crowns. According to some students of the <term>Ari<gloss>Rabbi Isaac Luria</gloss></term> and the <term>MaHaRShAL<gloss>Rabbi Solomon Luria, a 16th-century authority</gloss></term>, it should have two crowns.
**Leavened bread** (*Chametz*): On the letters *Tzadi*, *Dalet*, and *Kof*, there should be three crowns, and on the *Mem* there is one crown. Some say 30 crowns, which is the opinion of **Rashi** <note>The preeminent 11th-century commentator</note>. Accurate ancient books also specify 30 crowns. On the letter *Tzadi*, there should be five crowns, which is the universal opinion. According to the scribal traditions of the *Ari* and the *MaHaRShAL*, the letters *Cheit*, *Kof*, and *Nun* get five crowns, and the *Shin* and *Lamed* get five crowns.
**And the Jebusite** (*V'ha-Yevusi*): The letters *Zayin* and *Heh* get two crowns each. This is the opinion of the *MaHaRShAL* and the *Sefer ha-Tikkun*, as well as the **Tur** <note>The 14th-century code of Rabbi Jacob ben Asher</note>.
**Which** (*Asher*): In the *Tur*, section 8, it is written that the *Shin* of *Asher* gets two crowns. Others say five crowns, and so it is in the *Sefer ha-Scribim*. This is also the opinion of the **RoSh** <note>Rabbi Asher ben Yehiel</note>. According to the tradition of the *Ari* and the *MaHaRShAL*, it should have six crowns.
**To me** (*Li*): I found in my writings that there should be two crowns on the *Yod* and *Lamed*, and so on, during the preparation for all the verses. I also found in the tradition of the *Ari* and the *MaHaRShAL* that it should have three crowns.
**So that the Torah shall be** (*L'ma'an tihyeh torat*): The *Tur* says the three letters of the word *L'ma'an* (so that) get three crowns on each and every letter. This is also the tradition of the *Ari* and *MaHaRShAL* and the opinion of all the <term>Halakhic authorities<gloss>Posekim</gloss></term>. The two letters *Heh* of the word *Tihyeh* (shall be) according to the tradition of the *Ari* and *MaHaRShAL* get five crowns each. The two crowns of the word **Torah** (*Torat*) get three crowns each. This is the opinion of the *Ari*, the *MaHaRShAL*, and the *Tur*.
**Brought you out** (*Hotzi'acha*): I found written in ancient books that the letter *Heh* of *Hotzi'acha* gets four crowns. Likewise, the letter *Lamed* gets three crowns.
**At its appointed time** (*L'mo'adah*): I also found that the letter *Heh* of *L'mo'adah* gets three crowns.

# Laws of Tefillin

### Nine
Verses are found in the section <note>The section referred to is likely "And it shall come to pass if you obey" (Deuteronomy 11:13–21)</note> and seven [verses] corresponding to the "filling" of 360 <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of 360 corresponds to the Hebrew letters Shin and Samekh; this refers to Kabbalistic "spelling out" of divine names</note>. The lines of the columns are 360, containing nine letters. Furthermore, from the beginning of the portion, one must leave a blank space equivalent to the "filling" of nine letters. And so too, regarding the parchment, there are 107 letters in the lines corresponding to the "departure to the side" <note>A technical term for the margin or end of a line</note> whose sign is "taken" and at times 160.

### All the Verses
of the four portions [of the Tefillin] are 18 in number. This corresponds to the "filling" of the name [of God] and is the secret of the **Surrounding Light** <term>Or HaMakif: In Kabbalah, this refers to a divine energy that is too powerful to be internalized and instead surrounds the person</term> as will be explained later. However, the *Tallit* <note>Prayer shawl</note> is a much larger "Surrounding Light" than the Tefillin. Similarly, the "Surrounding Light" also includes two *Tallitot* <note>Plural of Tallit</note>.

### Deficient and Full Spellings
<note>Hebrew orthography often allows words to be written "full" (with extra vowels like Vav or Yod) or "deficient" (without them). In Tefillin, these spellings are legally binding and must be exact.</note>

**Hear** <note>original: "שמע" (Deuteronomy 6:4)</note> is deficient of a *Vav*. **My commandments** is full with a *Vav*. **First rain** is full with a *Vav*.
**And the latter rain** is full with a *Vav*. **And your wine** is deficient of a *Vav*.
**And you shall prostrate yourselves** is full with a *Vav*. **Its produce** is full with a *Vav*. **The good [land]** is deficient of a *Vav*.
**K'tan** <note>Meaning small; likely a reference to a specific word variant</note> is deficient of a *Vav*. **K'tam** is deficient of a *Vav*. **For a sign** is full with a *Vav*.
**For frontlets** <note>original: "לטוטפת"</note> is full with a *Vav*. **And for a sign** <note>The OCR reads "wedding" (l'chatunah), but contextually it is likely "frontlets"</note> is deficient of a *Vav*. **Your eyes**
is full with two *Yods*. **To them** is deficient of a *Vav*. In the "full" writing it has a *Yod*.
**To spare** is deficient of a *Yod* according to some. **And when you arise** is full with a *Vav*. **Doorposts**
is full with two *Vavs*. **Your house** is full with a *Yod* [creating a] wide [spacing]. **And in your gates**
is full with a *Yod*. **For your days** is deficient of a *Vav*.

### Crowns for the Portion "And It Shall Be"

**In its season** <note>original: "בעתו"</note>: In the *Tikkun K'hi* <note>A specific scribal manual</note>, there are seven crowns on the letter *Ayin*. However, it is not common to see this in the Tefillin of our teachers' students.
**And the latter rain** <note>original: "ומלקוש"</note>: My source <note>original: "מנחתי" (Minchati)</note> notes that in ancient Tefillin the letter *Kof* has three crowns.
**And you shall gather** <note>original: "ואספת"</note>: Three crowns on the letter *Peh*. There is a secret regarding the [letter] *Kof*. According to the Rambam <note>Maimonides, the 12th-century philosopher and legalist</note> and the *Tikkun K'hi*, there are also three crowns on the letter *Samekh*.
**Your grain** <note>original: "דגנך"</note>: Three crowns on the letter *Gimmel* and two crowns on the letter *Dalet* [following] the *Tur* <note>A code of Jewish law</note> section 18. And in the *Tikkun K'hi*, it is added that the *Kof* has three crowns on every side.
**And your wine** <note>original: "ותירשך"</note>: Three crowns on the letter *Resh*. Thus says my source, and so it is in the *Tikkun K'hi*.

**And your oil** <note>original: "ויצהרך"</note>: Two crowns on the letter *Dalet*. Thus says my source regarding precise Tefillin, and so it is in the *Tikkun K'hi*.
**Lest [your heart] be enticed** <note>original: "פן יפתה"</note>: The scribes who make the letter *Peh* "spiraled" <note>original: "מלופפת" (malofefet); a scribal tradition where the inner part of the letter Peh curls like a spiral</note> are holy. However, the majority do not do this at all, and certainly not in Tefillin. In the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letter *Peh* has lines, and the letter *Tav* of *yifteh* has two crowns on each side, and the [second] *Tav* of *yifteh* has two crowns.
**Was kindled** <note>original: "חרה"</note>: The prominent scribes are careful to make the letter *Chet* in this manner:
<image-desc>A scribal diagram showing the construction of the letter Chet (ח) formed by two Zayins joined at the top with a rounded bridge (hatoteret).</image-desc>
But the Sephardim <note>Jews of Spanish or North African descent</note> do not do this.
**The good** <note>original: "הטובה"</note>: In the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letter *Peh* has crowns.
**And you shall bind them** <note>original: "וקשרתם"</note>: The letter *Kof* has two crowns, as my source notes regarding precise Tefillin. And in the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letter *Shin* has six crowns.
**For frontlets** <note>original: "לטוטפת"</note>: Two [crowns on the] *Tet*, *Tet*. Each has three crowns according to the Rambam. If they have five crowns, two on each *Yod* and one on the staff, this also matches my source for precise Tefillin and the *Tikkun K'hi*. The letter *Peh* has three crowns.
**When you sit** <note>original: "בשבתך"</note>: In the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letter *Shin* has seven crowns.
**And when you arise** <note>original: "ובקומך"</note>: The letter *Kof* has two crowns. In the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letters *Kof* and *Mem* each have two crowns.
**The heavens** <note>original: "השמים"</note>: In the *Tikkun K'hi*, the letter *Shin* has seven crowns.
**The earth** <note>original: "הארץ"</note>: The letter *Tzadi* has three large crowns. In the *Tikkun K'hi*, it has six crowns—three on each side—and one on the staff. Regarding the [letter] *Aleph* in the word *Ha’aretz*, it is upright and has no crowns at all.

### Order of Wrapping the Portions
**One should roll** each portion from its end to its beginning, so that if one needs to read from it, they will not be forced to unroll the whole thing before reaching the text. This is what is meant by "it is yours," and it is a **Law given to Moses at Sinai** <term>Halakha LeMoshe MiSinai: A law that has no scriptural source but was passed down orally from Sinai</term>. One should wrap a small piece of parchment around them, though if they do not wrap it, it is not disqualified. Some are careful to wrap them with the hair of a kosher animal, but it is enough to use any animal provided it is a kosher species.

# Laws of Tefillin

Every letter **He** [ה] has three crowns, and this is proven in the *Tur* <note>The *Arba'ah Turim*, a foundational code of Jewish law by Rabbi Jacob ben Asher</note> in that place.
However, I have not seen this at all in some of the older Tefillin
from the early scribes.

**Yerekha** <note>original: *yerekha* (your thigh), referring to a specific word in the text</note> is written with a bent *Nun-Tzadi-Pe* [נצ״ף] and a bent *He* [ה].
Regarding letters requiring three crowns: this is the opinion of the *Tur*.
Our Master <note>Likely referring to Rabbeinu Bahya</note> says the letter *He* [ה] in *Yerekha* has 30 crowns. So too wrote our Master Bahya <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-14th century commentator</note> in his commentary and in the *Tikkun Ha-Hali* <note>Likely referring to a scribal manual or a Kabbalistic "Rectification" text</note>. And for those two letters, each letter should have three crowns. I found in the books of the ancients that the letter *He* [ה] has 60 crowns, and I also found this in the book *Ba'al Ha-Turim*. He wrote there (may his memory be a blessing): there are 60 crowns on the *He* [ה] of *Yerekha*, corresponding to the 60 joints in the limb <note>the arm/hand</note> upon which the Tefillin are placed.

->**And for frontlets** [*u-letotafot*] – the two letters *Tet* [ט] and every *He* [ה] have 60 crowns.<-

This is the opinion of the *Tur*, and also the opinion of the *Rammas* <note>Likely Rabbi Moshe Zacuto, a prominent Kabbalist</note>.
In the *Tikkun Ha-Hali*, it says the letter *Pe* [פ] has three crowns and the letter *Tav* [ת] has three crowns. The sign for this is "TT" <note>The two letters *Tet* in *Totafot*</note>; all the *Vavs* [ו] have crowns. Some make three crowns on the letter *Tet* [ט] according to the law of "Kahal" and three crowns according to the law of "Samal" <note>Scribal mnemonics for groups of letters that receive specific crown patterns</note.
And some make all eighteen letters [in a specific section] with 60 crowns each, as is the secret of the Sun.

**Our Master** Bahya wrote in the portion of *Le-khol ha-khon* <note>referring to a specific section of his commentary</note>: all these crowns indicate the Attribute of Justice, as you know. This is not the rule for a Torah scroll, but specifically for the law of Tefillin. And these are the words that are written "long" <note>extended letters to fill space</note>: the final *Mem* [ם] of the word *Ha-Katan*, and the letter *Yod* [י] of "Ploni," and the letter *He* [ה] of *Yerekha*, and the word *Totafot* in the section of *Yerekha*. These must be written long in several elevated places; therefore, these specific rules for crowns apply specifically to the Tefillin worn on the hand.

## Portion of Shema

**This portion** alludes to the "Crown of Kindness" [Chesed]... and it is "Open" <note>referring to a *Petuchah* paragraph, which begins on a new line</note> and its layout is simple.
In this portion, there are two Names [of God], and one must meditate on every "Existence" <note>the Tetragrammaton, which stems from the root "to be"</note> with the vowel points of *Malkhu* <note>the Sephirah of Kingship</note>, which is a crown for Kindnesses. One must also intend for the name *Y-S-V* and the name *L-M-L-K-V* to give life.

**Six** verses are in the portion of Shema, corresponding to the six directions <note>North, South, East, West, Up, Down</note>... and one should add to these six verses the five "Existences" <note>Divine Names</note> corresponding to the five Kindnesses. The end of every verse equals the numerical value of *Adonai* [Lord] to indicate unity. The first verse is the "Crown of Kindness," which is the male principle, for the female is always included within the male. Similarly, in this portion, there are 72 letters of the Divine Name, corresponding to the numerical value of *Chesed* [Kindness], which is 72 in total.

### Deficient and Full Spellings
<note>Hebrew scribal law is extremely strict about which words include "vowel-letters" (Vav and Yod). A "Full" (Malei) word has them; a "Deficient" (Chaser) word omits them.</note>

**Shema**: The letter *Ayin* [ע] is large. **Echad**: The letter *Dalet* [ד] is large.
**Me'odekha**: Missing a *Vav* [ו]. **Levavekha**: Full with a *Yod* [י]. **Bekhol-tekha**: Full with a *Yod* [י] in the first instance and full with a *Yod* [י] at the end. **U-ve-kumekha**: Full with a *Vav* [ו]. **Le-ot**: Full with a *Vav* [ו]. **Yadekha**: Missing a *Yod* [י]. **Letotafot**: Missing three *Vavs* [ו]. **Einekha**: Full with two *Yods* [י]. **Mezuzot**: Missing the *Vav* [ו] between the *Vav* and the *Zayin*, and the second *Vav* [ו] is full. **Beitekha**: Missing the second *Yod* [י]. **U-vish'arekha**: Full with a *Yod* [י]. All of this follows the opinion of the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the preeminent Kabbalist of Safed</note>, may his memory be a blessing.

## Crowns of the Shema Portion

**Shema**: The letter *Shin* [ש] of Shema has four crowns. However, I found in the *Tikkun Ha-Hali* that the letter *Shin* [ש] should have six crowns and the letter *Ayin* [ע] five crowns. According to the *Tur*, these two letters should not have them, but the *Shin* [ש] of Shema has three large crowns on each and every branch.

**Echad**: In the *Tikkun Ha-Hali*, the letter *Lamed* [ל]... has two crowns, and one must write the "heel" of the *Lamed* with thickness... as mentioned in the Laws of Tefillin.

**U-ve-kumekha**: The letter *Qof* [ק] has three crowns. In the *Tikkun Ha-Hali*, the letter *Qof* [ק] has three crowns and the letter *Mem* [מ] has three crowns. So I found in some of the older Tefillin.

**U-kshartam**: The letter *Qof* [ק] has three crowns according to the *Rammas*. In the *Tikkun Ha-Hali*, the letter *Qof* [ק] has three crowns and the letter *Tet* [ט] has seven crowns.

**Letotafot**: The two letters *Tet* [ט] have three crowns on each, according to the opinion of the *Tur*. But the *Rosh* <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel</note> disagrees. According to the *Rammas*, the letters *Tet-Tet-Pe* [טטפ] each have three crowns. In the *Tikkun Ha-Hali*, I found that for the two *Tets* [טט], each has seven crowns and the letter *Pe* [פ] has three crowns.

## Portion of "And it shall come to pass if you obey"

**This portion** alludes to the "Crown of Strength" [Gevurah]... and it is "Closed" <note>referring to a *Setumah* paragraph, which begins after a space on the same line</note>. In this portion, there are twenty-four Names [of God]... which is the "Crown of Strengths." One must meditate on the name *S-N* and the name *Malkhi* in its "filled" form...

# Laws of Tefillin

### Laws of the Crowns [Tagin]

**Sha’atnez Getz** <note>original: *Sha'atnez Getz* [שעטנז גץ], a mnemonic for the letters Shin, Ayin, Tet, Nun, Zayin, Gimel, and Tzadi</note>: these letters require three crowns to be made on each letter. **Bedek Hayah** <note>original: *Bedek Hayah* [בדק חיה], a mnemonic for the letters Bet, Dalet, Kuf, Het, Yod, and He</note>: these letters require one crown to be made on each and every letter, and afterward, these are [ready for] the Torah scrolls.
**These I take from the Scribe’s Scroll** <note>referring to *Hemdat Sofer*, a manual for scribes</note>: these are from *The Scribe’s Desire* regarding the letters; these are the letters of *The Scribe’s Desire* that require crowns. These are what the ancients wrote in detail as mentioned above. And for every **Name [containing the letter] Kuf** [ק] that one writes, you shall do thus: **Yedid** <note>meaning "Beloved" or "Friend"; here it refers to a specific mystical name or intention</note>, and so, a blessing shall come upon one who is stringent. And this is the general rule: all crowns must be [pointed] toward the top, for such is the Law given to Moses at Sinai. And all the additional crowns must also be toward the top. .
**Four** compartments <note>term: *batim* (houses), the leather boxes containing the scrolls</note> are in the Tefillin of the head. And just as there is one [compartment] in the Tefillin of the hand, and the eye <note>the scribe or wearer</note> added eight sections there, making five compartments and eight sections—their numerical value <note>term: *gematria*, the Jewish system of assigning numerical value to letters</note> is equal to "for one" [*le-echad*], to teach that the two Tefillin, of the head and of the hand, are equal in all their counts and rectifications. They all serve to indicate "One" [God], and their "eyes" [intentions] are as it was said: "Remember" and "Observe" were spoken in a single utterance <note>A reference to the two versions of the Fourth Commandment in the Ten Commandments, which tradition says were heard simultaneously</note>. Therefore, one must write both at the same time without any invalidating distraction at all. One’s intention should be precisely to join the Masculine and Feminine aspects [*Zun*] <note>Kabbalistic shorthand for *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, the divine archetypes</note> together, so that no "stranger" [impure force] shall intervene between them. .
**In the four** sections of the Tefillin, there are 450 words, and with the inclusion of the four sections themselves, they equal the numerical value of the word "Sign" [*Ot*]. This is [the meaning of] "And it shall be for a sign [*ot*] upon your hand." And if we divide the number of "Sign" before it—that is, if you count every letter before its essence in the gematria—the first sections have 250 words [and] 470 [letters?], which teaches us they are the "brains" and the "connectors" [*hushakim*]. In the last two sections, there are 119 words, which correspond to the Crown. The Names... that wander in the Knowledge of the "Small Face" [*Zeir Anpin*], which are two [measures of] Kindness [*Hasadim*] and three [measures of] Severity [*Gevurot*], making twelve sections; they are the three "brains" of the Lion, which are the Kindnesses and Severities. .
**And one must** write all four sections on a single parchment and wrap them from the end to the beginning as mentioned, and wrap hair over them. Over that, wrap a piece of kosher parchment, and then wrap hair over them again as mentioned above, and insert them into one compartment, as it is written: "And it shall be for a sign upon your hand"—"a sign" [singular] implies one. If they were [placed] within... parchments and both were in one compartment, he has fulfilled the obligation. One does not need to specifically seek the letter *He* [ה] since they are in one compartment. It is best to stick them together with wax so that the letter *Het* [ח] is on the outside, and thus the letter *Het* [ח] is added on the inside. It is better not to rely on the sellers of glue without supervision; one should make it himself from the scraps of leather remaining from the compartments, the parchments, and the straps, and this is undoubtedly kosher, and a blessing shall come upon the one who is stringent. . And after preparing the compartments in their place, whether for the head or the hand, place one parchment the width of the box to cover the opening of the sections at the bottom. They hinted that in the Tefillin of the hand, one should place one compartment because it alludes to the attribute of the Holy Sovereignty [*Malchut*], the Bride who is comprised of everything above her. Your mnemonic is: "My dove, my perfect one, is but one." .

These are indicated by the signs: the hair must be of a specific length and type. One must wash the hair thoroughly until it is smooth, so that it is separate and individual.
