# Laws of Tefillin

The arrangement of the sections <note>of the parchment</note> is a mystery and a sign, not to be heard <note>disclosed</note> lightly, therefore one must take care... and one must wear them as it is written, "for I have called for a portion," meaning a research of the bound elements together, therefore they are called "surroundings." The discussed section is called "the place to take." Therefore, if the hand-tefillin is not placed below and the head-tefillin in the upper pillar, it is considered a transgression <note>Hebrew: *averah*</note>. The explanation in the secrets of Unification is that if a "transgression" was in his hand, he shall not find rest. This refers to the curse mentioned in the first chapter of Tractate Menachot, which causes a person to lose what they have.

Rav Hisda said: An extra drop between one stitch and its neighbor causes a person to be moved <note>judged</note> at the time of death. And the Sabbath and the Covenant are like wives... and anyone who speaks during the act of binding <note>the tefillin</note> causes a separation between them, which is the "Name of the Grave," Death. This person sucks away all the abundance of the Kingdom <note>the *Shekhinah*</note>. For the intention, as written after the intention for donning tefillin, must be to focus on the Names: *Ehyeh, Havayah, Ehyeh, Adonai* <note>Divine Names associated with different spiritual realms</note>, which numerically equals "Life" <note>Hebrew: *Chayyim*</note>, for the tefillin are called the "Hand of the Living King."

Behold, one who engages in idle chatter between the two tefillin awakens Death in the place of Life. For him, it is not just a "transgression" but Death itself. As is known, the <term>Samael</term> <note>the primary angel of evil</note> is called "Dog," and <term>Lilith</term> <note>a female demonic figure</note> is called "Pig." Together, their numerical value equals "Transgression" <note>Hebrew: *Averah* = 277</note>. (There, the "transgression" was in his hand and he had no rest). This means that Samael and Lilith attach themselves to the hand-tefillin. This is why the text specifies "in his hand," for this causes Death to separate the "Holy Portion" from the "Life." Because of this, "a transgression was in his hand," and regarding such a person, they say "he returns from the battle lines" <note>referring to the Talmudic law that one who is fearful of his sins returns from war</note>. As we say in the chapter *Minchah*, it was a transgression, etc. Therefore, these things are "hindrances" that are specifically "in his hand" as mentioned. The one who corrects this will not die; meaning, if he went out to war at that hour, he would have died, Heaven forbid. Measure for measure: he awakened Death over Life, and correspondingly, he would die in battle.

The reason why he should specifically fear in war, and why they would return from the battle lines, and how this is "measure for measure," can be understood from what is written in the *Tikunei Zohar Chadash* (page 18, column 3): When a man places tefillin on his head, he intends to ascend all souls to Life under the authority of the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>, which is the head-tefillin... and to bring all the "hot tempers" of the world under the hand of the Lower *Shekhinah*. Because in exile, the "Slave" <note>the forces of impurity</note> rules under three legs...

<column-break/>

... "A slave when he reigns" <note>Proverbs 30:22</note>. And in everything, you should know why the family, etc., the Mistress, etc. The head-tefillin is the "Yod" above, placed under the Higher Mistress. Therefore, anyone who subjugates all the "hot tempers" of the world under the *Shekhinah* brings peace to the world. But those who wage war with the *Shekhinah* because they want to rule over Her, also awaken the "Slave" above and bring the "Name of the Grave," Death, upon the *Shekhinah*. Therefore, measure for measure, he also dies in war.

The R"CH <note>likely Rav Chayyim Vital or similar authority</note> wrote in the *Minor Laws*: What is the difference between one tefillin and the other? Because the commandment of the day is tefillin, its repair and its existence are like the "Wise Men of War" <note>referring to Gad in Deut. 33:20</note>, "He tears the arm and also the crown of the head." There is no name there but holiness, and to act for the sake of the "Nothingness" <note>*Ayin*</note>, one must not interrupt.

Now we must understand why specifically a blessing is required... for "He tears the arm and also the crown of the head." The reason is according to what our Sages of blessed memory said: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon thee, and they shall be afraid of thee" <note>Deut. 28:10</note>. This refers to the letter *Shin* on the tefillin. Behold, the six *Shins* <note>the three-headed and four-headed Shins on the head-tefillin</note>... which correspond to the four chains... and correspond to the "Minds of Greatness" and "Minds of Smallness" <note>Kabbalistic states of consciousness</note> that are in the head-tefillin and the hand-tefillin. They are the letters *Gimel-Lamed* <note>revealed</note>... and this is why the blessing requires more focus than other blessings. If they are not worthy of the blessing, it is in vain.

And what was said about "taking for a son," this refers to the *Tzadik* <note>the Righteous One/Foundation</note>, which is the Sabbath day—"Remember" and "Observe" in a single utterance. This means that the awakening and the submission are each on their own... and all are joined together in the *Yesod* <note>Foundation</note> which is the *Tzadik*. Through him, the *Shekhinah* is made one in a single unity, a complete Life of the Name *Havayah*... and this is for the sake of the "Son of God." I have heard that in this section, the numerical value of *Havayah* is found... to remember the Names to strengthen them. For everything from the side of the Right and the Left shall be established, both of them being two commandments. They are from the "Arrangement of Light." Generally, the head-tefillin is called the "Tefillin of the Most High," and it is called the "First Commandment." Afterward, the discourse concludes: in this manner are all the commandments. And because of this, there is a dispute between the Braaitot <note>early oral traditions</note> regarding tefillin and other commandments, between the Right and the Left, for there, there is no unity for them.

# Laws of Tefillin

to the "crown of the covering" <note>original: *itura de-matleya*</note> as our Sages of blessed memory said. Therefore, the opinion of Rabbenu Tam <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Meir, 12th-century French Tosafist</note> is that the order of the scrolls should be: *Sanctify (Kadesh)*, *And it shall come to pass (Ve-haya)*, *Hear (Shema)*, and *And it shall come to pass if you hearken (Ve-haya im shamoa)*. The custom and the sections must be placed so that the *Hear (Shema)* section comes before the *And it shall come to pass (Ve-haya)* section. However, the Ra’avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David, 12th-century critic of Maimonides</note> of blessed memory intended another reason, based on the "voice of the streams of the head" <note>a mystical reference to the flow of divine intellect</note>, that the scrolls should be placed so that the "Kindness" <note>Chesed</note> goes to the right and "Strength" <note>Gevurah</note> to the left. And also the "voice of the kings" to the right arm which is necessary. Therefore, also in the Tefillin, the "Branch of Wisdom" <note>Chokhmah</note> is found on the right of the *Zeir Anpin* <note>The "Small Face" or emotive attributes of God in Kabbalah</note> for all life, and from the "Crown of Light" before the "Crown of the Covering." For this reason, the opinion of the Ra’avad is that *Sanctify (Kadesh)* is on the right of the person wearing them, and the "Husks" <note>Kelipot/impurities</note> are in the middle. However, this is a rejected opinion. Since the writing of the scrolls on the right was abolished, and the external "Husks" which descend into the secret of the scrolls in the custom of *Zeir Anpin* are also abolished at this time, no life remains except in the writing of the Tefillin. Therefore, we do not make Tefillin according to the Ra’avad, and the law is not like him in this matter. However, regarding the opinions of the Geonim <note>Leaders of Babylonian academies</note>, Rashi, and Rabbenu Tam, they are all true and one must fulfill them all. That is to say, in the morning one must wear Rashi and Rabbenu Tam together, as will be explained later in the "Great Service" <term>Shimusha Rabba: An ancient manual on the construction and wearing of Tefillin</term>. And the "Great Service" Tefillin should be worn during the Afternoon Prayer <note>Mincha</note>, because these Tefillin fulfill both the opinions of Rashi and Rabbenu Tam. That is, regarding the *Sanctify (Kadesh)* being on the right of the wearer, it hints at the brains of the "Father" <note>Abba/Chokhmah</note> which is on the right of the "Long Face" <note>Arich Anpin</note> as mentioned; and regarding the sections being in their order, it hints at the brains of the "Mother" <note>Imma/Binah</note>. Therefore, the size of these is "four fingers by four fingers" <note>approx. 8x8 cm</note>, and the reason is explained in the chapter "The Fold" <note>Menachot 35a</note> regarding Tefillin: since we say there is room on the head to wear two pairs of Tefillin, and between them there is enough space for two fingers, it is proven that the place of Tefillin is four fingers wide. His reasoning was that since between the hair-line and the crown of the head is the house of the Tefillin, that place is two fingers wide in the manner of the brain. Thus, when you make them four fingers by four fingers, they correspond to the two brains—the "Father" <note>Abba</note> corresponding to two fingers, and the "Mother" <note>Imma</note> corresponding to two fingers. Therefore, he wrote that one who makes them should make them two fingers [wide], and if we make them larger, it is even better, provided they are not less than that. And so it is proven in the *Tosafot* <note>medieval commentaries</note> on the chapter "The Handful" <note>Menachot</note> page 34b, see there. And the holiness of our Tefillin is such that one can wear them according to Rashi and bless upon them the Name of God, as stated in the *Mishneh Torah*, Laws of Prayer, Chapter 4, that one should wear the Tefillin of Rashi, and so wrote our Rabbi [Maimonides] there. And so

# The Order of Placing the Sections in the Tefillin According to
# Rashi, of Blessed Memory, and the Ra'avad, and the Shimusha
# Rabba, and They are Two that are Four <note>A Talmudic expression meaning two primary categories that expand into four sub-categories</note>

### How so?
For Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (1040–1105), the primary commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note> believes that the section "Sanctify" <note>Exodus 13:1-10</note> is on the left of the one wearing them. Similarly, Rabbenu Tam believes "Sanctify" is on the left of the wearer. Thus, they both share one opinion regarding the section of "Sanctify"—that it must specifically be on the left of the wearer. However, the Ra'avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David (1125–1198)</note> and the *Shimusha Rabba* <note>An early medieval work on the laws of Tefillin</note> disagree on this <unclear>decree</unclear> of the Blessed One; they believe that the section of "Sanctify" must be on the **right** of the wearer. Thus, there are "two that are four" regarding the internal arrangement. Furthermore, there are two doubts regarding the two sections "Hear" <note>Deuteronomy 6:4-9</note> and "And it shall come to pass if you surely listen" <note>Deuteronomy 11:13-21</note>—which one should be on the outside? Behold, the *Shimusha Rabba* and Rashi believe that the way to write them and place the sections is in their chronological order <note>The order they appear in the Torah</note>, as the order of the Divine Name <term>Havayah</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, Y-H-V-H</note> is most perfectly made this way. But the Ra'avad and Rabbenu Tam believe that while one must write them in their chronological order, when placing them in the leather boxes, one must put the "Havayahs" in the middle: "Sanctify," "And it shall be when He brings you," "Hear," and "And it shall come to pass if you surely listen" <note>This refers to the specific arrangement where the two sections containing the name of God are adjacent in the center</note>.

### And it Appears
That one Master said one thing, and the other Master said another, and they do not actually disagree, for "both these and those are the words of the Living God" <note>A Talmudic phrase indicating that multiple conflicting views can hold spiritual truth</note. One must first provide an introduction regarding what the Rabbi <note>Likely referring to Isaac Luria, the "Ari," 1534–1572</note>, of blessed memory, established: that the <term>Mochin</term> <note>Mental/Intellectual faculties in Kabbalah</note> of <term>Abba</term> <note>The Father/Wisdom aspect</note> emerge in the aspect of Understanding in the forehead for this, and the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Imma</term> <note>The Mother/Understanding aspect</note> emerge in the aspect of the Tefillin in the forehead for that. Behold, the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Abba</term> would pierce the <unclear>space</unclear> in the forehead, for the revelation of the forehead only serves to empower it. And behold, it is the <term>Sefirah</term> of Wisdom and the Kindnesses of the <term>Da'at</term> (Knowledge) on the right side, and the Darkness of Understanding and the Strengths on the left side, and they all spread throughout the forehead and became the aspect of the body of <term>Nukva</term> <note>The Feminine aspect</note>. And so it was written: the Name <term>Havayah</term> from above, *Yah* on the right and *Heh* on the left, and the extension of its Wisdom was over the entire forehead. And previously it was written: "the sweetness of a kiss, my brother." But the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Imma</term> are arranged: "Sanctify" and "And it shall be when He brings you" on the right of the wearer, and "Hear" and "And it shall come to pass if you surely listen" on the left of the wearer. However, at the time when the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Abba</term> mix with the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Imma</term> in order to emerge in the aspect of Tefillin, the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Abba</term> are forced into the head; "Sanctify" is on the right of the forehead, but "And it shall come to pass if you surely listen"

rests before the section of "Hear." Therefore, these four aspects correspond to the intentions of the four souls of the world. First, one must know that <term>Abba</term> clothes the right arm of <term>Arich Anpin</term> <note>The "Long Face," representing Divine Will/Patience</note>, and <term>Imma</term> clothes the left arm of <term>Arich Anpin</term>. Now, even though through the power of <term>Imma</term>, it clothes the entire right line of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> <note>The "Small Face," representing the emotive attributes</note>, and the Splendor of <term>Imma</term> clothes the entire left line of <term>Zeir Anpin</term>, it would be appropriate for Wisdom to be on the right of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> and subsequently Understanding and Strength on the left of <term>Zeir Anpin</term>. But since it is impossible for the <term>Mochin</term> to emerge and bulge from the forehead of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> except through the "hardness of the hair-strand" of <term>Arich Anpin</term> which merits the nape of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> and pushes the inner <term>Mochin</term> outward into the forehead of <term>Zeir Anpin</term>—and it is known that the Strength of <term>Atik</term> <note>The "Ancient One," the highest level of the Divine</note> which was in the "Chest of the Flint" is clothed within the Understanding of <term>Arich Anpin</term>, and from there emerged the hardness of the hair-strand for <term>Zeir Anpin</term> which clothes them, and not the Strength in Wisdom—therefore Wisdom is called "black" as mentioned in the Zohar, portion of *Pinchas* in the *Raya Mehemna*. And since the Tefillin emerge via the hardness of the hair-strand, it causes the Wisdom of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> to also rest on his left side. Therefore, one must place Wisdom on the left of the wearer, and afterwards Understanding (which is Kingship and the left arm of <term>Arich Anpin</term>), and afterwards the Kindnesses, and <unclear>finally</unclear> the Strengths. This is as mentioned in the explanation of "These are the Gods," and this is the opinion of Rashi, of blessed memory: "Sanctify" is on the left of the wearer and the sections are in their chronological order. However, the *Shimusha Rabba* intended another reason: that the power of <term>Imma</term> clothes the right line of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> and the Splendor of Understanding clothes the left line of <term>Zeir Anpin</term>; therefore, when the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Zeir Anpin</term> emerge, they emerge in order as they stand, which is Wisdom on the right of <term>Zeir Anpin</term>, then Understanding, then Kindnesses, then Strengths. Therefore, the *Shimusha Rabba* believes "Sanctify" must be on the right of the wearer, but the sections remain in chronological order. This is the dispute regarding all "Rashi Tefillin," which correspond to <term>Imma</term>. But regarding the intention of all: Behold, Rabbenu Tam intended another reason, which is that even though in the aspect of the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Abba</term> there is a *Yod* on the right and a *Heh* on the left, nevertheless, later when they emerge in the aspect of the <term>Mochin</term> of Tefillin, then the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Abba</term> also emerge according to the order of the <term>Mochin</term> of <term>Imma</term>, since the aspect of <term>Abba</term> is clothed within the aspect of <term>Imma</term>... therefore one must place "Sanctify" on the left of the wearer, but the Names <note>Havayah</note> in the middle, so that by joining them, the stature of Israel is remembered.

However, since it is impossible to bring down the Mentalities <term>Mochin; divine intellectual energies</term> to be prominent in the place of the Small Face except through the "Hair-Combings" <term>Kuzah Chuzra; a specific Kabbalistic metaphor for the transmission of light</term> of the hair of the Long Face which strikes the nape of the Small Face, and this causes the inner Mentalities to emerge outward in the place of the Small Face. It is known that the Strength of the "Ancient One" <term>Atik; the most hidden Divine aspect</term>... is clothed within the Wisdom of the Long Face, and from there the "Hair-Combings" are placed... and through the clothing of this Strength in Wisdom to Understanding... as explained in the *Zohar* in the portion of *Phinehas* (page 248). 

And since the Tefillin draw sustenance through these "Hair-Combings," therefore the form of the Wisdom of the Small Face is also placed on his left side. Therefore, one must place Wisdom on the left of the wearer, and afterwards Understanding, which was the Sovereignty and left arm of the Long Face, and the Kindness of Kindnesses and the Kindness of Strengths. This is seen in the explanation of the Rabbi in *Lekutei Torah*, and this is the opinion of Rashi, of blessed memory, who ruled that the wearer places the sections in their chronological order as written in the Torah.

But the system of Rabbeinu Tam <note>Rashi's grandson, who famously disagreed on the order of the scrolls</note> aimed at another reason: that the <unclear>presence</unclear> of the Mother clothes the right line of the Small Face, and Majesty to Understanding in the left line of the Small Face. Therefore, when the Mentalities descend to the Small Face, they are placed in their natural order in their standing place: namely, Wisdom on the right, then Understanding, then the Kindnesses, and then the Strengths. Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam's system holds that *Kadesh* <note>The first section: "Sanctify to Me..."</note> must be on the right of the wearer. But the sections themselves remain in their order. This is the dispute regarding the "Dew of Tefillin" <note>A mystical term for the influence within the scrolls</note> of Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam regarding the Mother. 

However, in the Mentalities of the Father <term>Abba; the Divine masculine/intellectual principle</term>, there is another reason... since the Wisdom of the Father is clothed within the Wisdom of the Mother... as written below regarding the portion of *Kadesh* in the Unification. Therefore, one must place *Kadesh* on the left of the wearer. But the Divine Names (*Havayot*) should not move...

<column-break/>

->The order of placing the sections in the Tefillin according to<-
## Rashi, Targum Yonatan, the Ra'avad, and the Shimmusha
### Rabba—which are two that are four

How so? For Rashi holds that *Kadesh* is on the left of the wearer, and likewise *Ve-hayah Ki Yevi'akha* <note>The second section: "And it shall be when He brings you..."</note> is next to *Kadesh* on the left of the wearer. Thus, there is one order for writing: the sections *Kadesh* and *Ve-hayah* are on the outer left of the wearer. You will find *Kadesh*... and your sign for this is <note>The text provides a mnemonic device</note>. And they differ in this: some believe the section of *Kadesh* must be on the right of the wearer. <unclear>In the explanation</unclear>... there are also two additional sections, which are the two portions of *Shema* and *Ve-hayah Im Shamoa* <note>The third and fourth sections</note>... and Rashi holds they are written in the order they appear in the Torah, which is the order of the Divine Names written in the *Zohar*. But the Ra'avad and Rabbeinu Tam hold that they must be arranged in their order, but to place them one needs the Divine Names... *Kadesh*, *Ve-hayah Im Shamoa*, and *Ve-hayah Ki Yevi'akha*.

And it appears that "this Master said one thing and that Master said another," and they do not actually conflict, for "both are the words of the Living God." One must first provide an introduction: what are the signs here and why? Because the Mentalities of the Father draw sustenance in the aspect of "Preparation" when placed for the Small Face, and the Mentalities of the Mother draw sustenance in the aspect of "Tefillin" when placed for the Small Face. And behold, the Mentalities of the Father would burst through... in the place of the Small Face... but their transmission is placed... Wisdom and Kindnesses emerging from the right side, and Understanding and Strengths from the left side. And they were all spreading throughout the placement... and so the Divine Name was written from above: *Yod-He* on the right and *Vav-He* on the left... written above in a single line. 

But the Mentalities of the Mother draw sustenance: *Kadesh* and *Ve-hayah Ki Yevi'akha* on the right of the wearer, and *Shema* and *Ve-hayah Im Shamoa* on the left of the wearer. However, at the time when the Mentalities of the Father mix with the Mentalities of the Mother in order to descend into the aspect of Tefillin for the "Unification of Mentalities," the Father's portion of *Kadesh* is on the right of the wearer. But *Ve-hayah Im Shamoa*...

# Laws of Tefillin

->The Hand-Tefillin<-

Without [interruption], he took hold of the royal garment, which is the Tefillin of the hand <note>The author uses "royal garment" as a metaphor for the Tefillin worn on the arm</note> below, and it shall truly be in service as mentioned above, for there is no deep opening with him as mentioned above. And truly, one must put on the Tefillin of the hand while sitting, according to the secret of "And the Ancient of Days sat" <note>Daniel 7:9</note>, as the Rabbi of blessed memory wrote in the *Book of Enoch* <note>A mystical reference</note>... in the seventh rectification. Therefore, one does not need to stand at the time of the blessing and the tying.

<column-break/>

So too, to tie while sitting, both the blessing and the tying are all while sitting. And one must learn a "light and heavy" <term>Kal V'Chomer: a logical inference from a minor case to a major one</term> deduction from the *Shema* prayer, which is a Torah obligation and contains the "Acceptance of the Yoke [of Heaven]." How much more so, by a "light and heavy" deduction, regarding the blessing for "putting on the Tefillin" of the hand, for it is a single mention [of God's name] and the Tefillin of the hand is in the World of Creation—how much more so must one also say the blessing while sitting. And anyone who stands at the time of the blessing, it is an error in his hand, and he does not perform the rectification of the Hand-Tefillin according to its proper design. And as for what the *Beit Yosef* <note>Rabbi Joseph Karo</note> brings in *Tur* section 8 in the name of the *Orchot [Chaim]*... that in the Jerusalem Talmud it says "all blessings are [performed] standing"—this refers to blessings over commandments <note>Mitzvot</note> and not blessings over pleasures, these are his words. And it seems to me that what he said about needing to stand for blessings over commandments refers specifically to blessings that are in the "World of Emanation" <note>Atzilut—the highest world</note>. But blessings that are in the "World of Creation," certainly the Jerusalem Talmud would agree that one specifically must say them while sitting, for one can learn the "light and heavy" deduction from the *Shema* etc. And the wise man... in the book *Ali Zaken* wrote as follows: "I am astonished at the *Beit Yosef* who wrote in the name of the Jerusalem Talmud that 'all blessings are standing,' for I have searched and this thing is not found in the Jerusalem Talmud."

And in my humble opinion, he wrote according to the secret of the Ramban <note>Nachmanides</note> in the portion of *Shoftim*... that one must put on the Hand-Tefillin while sitting. And he writes... the version of the prayers... and it seems to me according to the hint... the word "and he sits" <note>original: *v'yoshev* (ויושב)</note>... the filling of the letters alone has the numerical value of "Sovereignty" <note>Malchut</note> to show that everything that is in the World of Creation must be done while sitting. And yet another reason according to what is said <margin>2</margin> in the Holy Zohar, portion *Vayechi* page 137b, as follows: "And the Ancient of Days sat upon this throne." Why is it written? If the Ancient of Days did not sit upon this throne, the world would not be able to exist before this throne, and when the Ancient of Days sits upon it...

# Laws of Tefillin

We have recorded at length in the *Secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him* <note>original: "Sod Hashem Liyre'av," a reference to Psalm 25:14 and often a title for mystical commentaries</note> regarding the secret of the Divine Face. Know that according to the secret, the Name of God has the aspect of a "Slam" <note>a kabbalistic cipher</note>, which is the secret of "Salsi" in a square formation, numerically equivalent to 151. Just as Israel was armed when they went out of Egypt—as it is written, "and the children of Israel went up armed" <note>Exodus 13:18</note>—so in the future shall this "H" be revealed, the inhabitant of the Ancient Ones, and they shall emerge from the shells <note>term: Kelipot (husks/shards of evil)</note>. The "Complete Redemption" has the numerical value of 149, and it shall be fulfilled in the days of "hiddenness," just as we saw in the land of Egypt. In the exile of the twenty provinces, which are the provinces of hardship, the letter "H" was swept away; but it shall be fulfilled on the Sabbath of this Palace, "You shall return, every man to his heritage."

## And afterward, before you recite the blessing for the Tefillin of the Hand, which is "to lay Tefillin":

After the Tefillin is already placed upon the muscle of the arm, but before you fasten it, you should direct this intention. First, intend toward what we explained above: that the Tefillin of the Hand represents the "Speech" of the Divine, while the Tefillin of the Head represents the "Thought." These are the repairs one performs in the Upper Worlds. Afterward, intend toward the unification of the Tefillin, which begins with the first letter. One must intend that if any blemish was caused to the "House" of the Tefillin, he now intends to unify the "Living One" <note>Chai</note> to repair that blemish. This is the intention:

**Intend** to connect the two letters *Yod* and *Heh*, which is the union of the "World of the Hidden" for the sake of the "World of the Revealed," a union meant to draw the "Brains" <note>term: Mochin (divine intellectual energies)</note> outward, for from these Brains the Tefillin emerge, as is known. Afterward, intend to raise the "Lower Heh" with the "Vav," which is the secret of the Kingdom <note>term: Malchut</note> rising to the level of Understanding <note>term: Binah</note> to be sustained by it. Then intend for the first "Dalet" regarding the final "Yod-Heh," which is the entry of the Brains through the miracle of the first "Heh" into the head of the Divine Couple. The blemish mentioned in the *Tikunei Zohar* is not to intend only to bring down the final "Heh" to the "Vav" alone; rather, one must remember all these "Houses" as *Yod-Heh, Heh-Vav, Heh-Vav*. This is the "Filling of the Name Sag" <note>a specific expansion of the four-letter Name of God totaling 63</note> which provides the life-force that brings forth the Tefillin. As stated in the *Tikunim* and the *Zohar*, the Tefillin are the "Mother" hovering over the "Son." (Note: The numerical value of the filling of the letters *Lamed*, *Vav*, and *Yod* is 156, which is the secret of the life-force found in the Foundation of the World of Formation, from which the Houses of the Tefillin emerge.) Intend that through this unification...

# Laws of Tefillin

One should focus the mind on the four names of the Lord <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note> in their "full" spellings, which equal the numerical values of 72, 63, 45, and 52 <note>These represent different levels of divine emanation: Ab, Sag, Mah, and Ben</note>. This corresponds to the "Brain of Wisdom" <term>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah, representing intuitive flash</term>, just as one intends during the reading of the Shema and according to the secret tradition.
**And afterwards**, one intends the four names of "I Will Be" <note>Hebrew: *Ehyeh*, associated with the higher realm of Keter/Binah</note> which are the first Sephirot. The first is spelled with the letter *Yod*, the third with *Aleph*, and all four involve the spellings of *Heh* and *Tet*—this constitutes the "Brain of Understanding" <term>Binah: the third Sephirah, representing analytical processing</term>. It is good to interweave them together: the first name of the Lord with the first name of *Ehyeh*, and so on for all the other combinations, to connect each perfect name with its companion.
**And afterwards**, you shall intend between the thirty names, which is the "filling" of the name *E-H-V-H* <note>A variation of the divine name</note> for the Head-Tefillin. For the letter *Yod*, focus on Kindness <term>Chesed</term> alone. But for the Hand-Tefillin, one must intend the word "Tefillin" with the letters *Yod* and *Dalet* <note>referring to the knot shapes</note> as explained in the verses.
**However**, regarding the eight names for the reading of the Shema of the *Mazal* <note>Destiny/Source</note>, the Rabbi <note>Maimonides</note> of blessed memory wrote that besides five for the Kindness of the Lord, one must intend them. This is even more certain from the words of my Master <note>Isaac Luria, the Ari</note>, of blessed memory, that one only needs a single intention for the "Two Brains" of Wisdom and Understanding, according to the secret of the Book <note>The Zohar</note>, encompassing the Name in the word "One" (*Echad*) in the Shema.
**And afterwards**, you shall intend the "Two Crowns" <note>referring to the straps or the letters on the boxes</note> corresponding to the name *Ehyeh* in its *Yod* spelling as well; this is the secret of the "Shin" on the houses <note>The letter Shin embossed on the Head-Tefillin</note>.
**And afterwards**, intend generally that these three names—*Ehyeh*, *Havayah* (the Lord), and *Ehyeh*—in their simple forms have the numerical value of 40 (*Mem*), and "Voice" (*Kol*) has the value of "Life" (*Chayim*), which are the secret of the Tefillin as mentioned in previous lessons. They also equal "Understanding" (*Binah*) with the inclusion of the word itself, for all this is the secret of the Tefillin mentioned above.
**And afterwards**, as I have already promised the prayer of Rabbi Shalom Sharabi <note>RASHASH</note>, you shall join the totality of the names of the Head <note>numerical value 420</note> and the totality of the names of the Hand, which equals the value of *Yabok* <note>112</note>. Thus, both together equal 160, the value of three Names of the Lord (72, 63, 45).
(The Rabbi <note>Ramaz</note> also wrote: "And this name is within it.")

# Laws of Tefillin

The author of *Lehaqah* <note>likely a reference to a specific Kabbalistic work or author</note> and the late Rabbi of Karydos Habib, of blessed memory, as well as the commentary on the tractate *Menachot*, all state that a scribal error should be corrected. This is because such errors hinder the fulfillment of the commandment, and one must protest against them. If someone takes out the Head-Tefillin before completing the binding of the Hand-Tefillin upon the bicep <term>the muscle of the upper arm where the Hand-Tefillin is placed</term> and the formation of the letter *Shin*... and the reason is as explained in the words of the Rabbi of *Lehaqah*. For the essence is that the heart is drawn after its actions, and this impression remains upon him at night like a "Surrounding Light" <term>Ohr Makif: a Kabbalistic concept of divine energy that surrounds rather than permeates</term>. Thus, you must ensure the Tefillin appear properly prepared with all their requirements, including the seven wraps. Afterward, he should place the Head-Tefillin. This is contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Zalman and Rabbenu Yerucham, of blessed memory, who say that the wraps are not an essential part of the commandment of placing Tefillin. However, according to the Rabbi of *Lehaqah*, it is the opposite: the seven wraps are indeed part of the commandment, as they represent the seven lower emanations <term>Sefirot</term> or the seven witnesses, as mentioned in *Lehaqah*. The author of *Luchot HaBerit* <note>Isaiah Horowitz, the Shelah HaKadosh</note> wrote similarly in his commentary on tractate *Chullin*, page 120b.

# Laws of Tefillin

### The middle [joint] and two on the lower joint:

**The secret** is as follows: It is known that the *Keter* <note>Crown; the highest Sefirah</note> is the secret of the "Encompassing Light" and is not considered part of the body, for "our Crown" is as the Sages of blessed memory said, "surrounding the world as a whole." Within the "garment" of the Crown, there are "matured brains" <note>intellectual faculties/mochin</note>, and those brains within it are very, very exalted; they are above the brains of *Zeir Anpin* <note>The "Small Face" or Microprosopus, representing the emotional attributes of God</note>. However, as the Rabbi <note>Isaac Luria, the Ari</note> wrote in *Likkutei Torah* on the Gate of the Cantillations, the numerical value of *Wisdom* (Chokhmah), *Understanding* (Binah), and *Knowledge* (Da'at) equals *Crown* (Keter).

And the Rabbi has already explained in the name of the *Kanah* <note>A classic Kabbalistic work</note> of blessed memory, explaining every point that the Holy One, Blessed be He, engages in, because the "brains" are in thirds—specifically the three thirds which are Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge, which includes the Kindnesses and Severities. These four brains become four square *Vavs* <image-desc>a small square outline representing a kabbalistic diagram</image-desc> and they become the "closed Mem" <note>The final form of the Hebrew letter Mem (ם)</note> of the word *L'marbeh* <note>Isaiah 9:6</note>, which serves the one called "Occupied with this" in the *Tikunim* at the beginning of Tikun 5, page 15. And behold, this shall be revealed through Kindness. Since it has already been drawn from the "Whiter Mazal" <note>A high level of Divine influence</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, engages and reveals it in the middle finger. There, the three brains are revealed at the end of the finger, which is the "Knowledge" (Da'at) mentioned by the Sages.

It is known that *Knowledge* (Da'at) is always higher than *Kindness* and *Severity*, just as *Foundation* (Yesod) is higher than *Victory* and *Splendor*. Therefore, one must make one wrap on the middle joint, which represents *Knowledge* that includes both Kindnesses and Severities together. On the lower joint, one makes two wraps corresponding to the *Kindness* and *Severity* of *Zeir Anpin* as they branch out into the worlds. Corresponding to these three wraps are the three phrases "And I will betroth you": two in the first verse and one in the second verse, which is *Knowledge*. Therefore, when making these three wraps on the finger, it is proper to say:

> And I will betroth you to Me forever;
> and I will betroth you to Me in righteousness, 
> and in justice, and in lovingkindness,
> and in compassion. And I will betroth you 
> to Me in faithfulness;
> and you shall know the Lord. <note>Hosea 2:21-22</note>

### A Second Reason

Based on what is mentioned in the *Zohar*, Volume III, page 142b: "And she began with the travels of the Book to spread to all and to be rectified with its rectifications, to be rectified in the covering of the Father and Mother <note>Abba and Imma</note> (the explanation is that it is a covering for the life of the world of Father and Mother, like the secret of the connection mentioned in the Zohar, portion Balak, page 210b, to give

<column-break/>

to David, and he rectified it wonderfully to be called by the name of Joseph. For the 'Crown of the Foundation' <note>Atarah of Yesod</note> is like a neck... and a covering for the Foundation of *Zeir*, see there). And behold, it is like the 'fat of its mother's milk' <note>a mystical metaphor</note> for the Mother is the 'World of Fifty Gates,' and it is drawn into the 'mouth of the Mother' which is called the letter *Yod*. And once the *Yod* is revealed in the mouth of the Mother, the 'Higher Witness' is revealed, etc." All these matters regarding the letter *Yod* should be guarded; see there. For through his blessings, he shall be for the worlds to come and shall be clarified in the "Lot of Life," full of his blessings, as it is written: "And upon all, all, all," and it is written: "And he engraved the Heavens for him between the eyes, perfectly revealed in the *Yod*." And to be guarded from poverty. Thus far his words. And although the verse refers to the "Covenant," it is because of this that he merited the letter *Yod*, as mentioned in the Zohar, portion Phinehas, page 210b. This is the meaning of "And Phinehas took a spear (*Romach*) in his hand," meaning he took the reception of the 248 (*Rmach*) worlds that are revealed in the *Yod*, which is the secret of the "Higher Crown," and he merited the blessings of the Lord. Therefore Phinehas merited to be included in the "Lot of Life" and did not die, and thus he lives in the Garden of Eden. We learn from here that holiness is in the "Mazal" of the letter *Yod*, and the "Crown" (Atarah) within us is the letter *Yod*, and it is in the Mazal of 7. This is what the Rabbi supported in *Likkutei Torah* in the "Discourse on the Wraps," saying: "You wrapped in the secret of the seventh, because the Foundation (Yesod) is the secret of the sevenfold, as is known. Therefore the angels say in that world which is 'entirely Sabbath and rest for the life of the worlds,' for it is the seventh of the Sabbath, the secret of the Foundation of the Holy One, Blessed be He, the 'Life of the Worlds'." Thus far his words. And as mentioned, there is another reason known from the "Discourse on the Husks" (*Kelipot*): for all six days of the week, the "Glow Husk" (*Kelipat Nogah*) covers the Foundation of *Zeir*... and every time Israel performs the commandment of circumcision below, the "Holy Crown" is elevated above... and therefore for *Zeir*, all six days of the week he has no connection with the lower Foundation, except on his Sabbath when the husk departs entirely. Then the Crown shines, which is the *Yod* on the letter *Yod* which is in the Mazal of 7. This is "a world that is entirely Sabbath and rest for the life of the worlds," for on the Sabbath there is rest for the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds" <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> from the *Nogah* so that it does not suckle from him. And this is the eternal connection. This is why the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) is called "Bathsheba" (Daughter of Seven), meaning she was a house and a garment... for the finger which is the sign of the Holy Covenant, which is in the strength of 7.

# Laws of Phylacteries

The wrapping is done on the lower joint of this finger <note>the middle finger</note>, specifically the joint closest to the palm of the hand. This is unlike the custom of the Priests, who wrap three times on the lower joint of the finger.

Nathan <note>likely the scribe or a student</note> says: It seems to me that we must understand what the Master <note>Isaac Luria, the "Ari"</note> wrote in the *Book of Reincarnations*, Chapter 15.

His words are as follows: The matter concerns the time of the Betrothal <term>Kiddushin: the first stage of a Jewish marriage where the groom sanctifies the bride</term> when a man sanctifies a woman. At that time, the woman is the secret of a "Surrounding Light" <term>Makif: a spiritual energy that encompasses rather than enters a vessel</term> from the "End of the Heights" <note>original: *NHY*, an acronym for the lower three spiritual emanations</note> of her husband's spirit. When he later enters her, he gives her an "Inner Spirit" <term>Pnimi: internal spiritual energy</term>, which is the secret of the Name of Forty-Two <note>a mystical name of God</note>, as is known, and this is internal. From the "Voice of the Spirit" that he placed in her at the time of the Betrothal, that very essence becomes the secret of a surrounding shell for that Inner Spirit. If he had not given her the Betrothal, it would not have been possible for that Inner Spirit to enter her. These are his words.

Now we must understand how the "Surrounding Light" of the Betrothal, which he places on her finger, connects with the "Internal Vessel" that is in her middle finger. For this reason, he places the Betrothal ring on her finger called the *Ammah* <note>the middle finger; literally "cubit"</note>. This is because the Bride is compared to the "filling" of the finger, as mentioned by the Sages of blessed memory regarding the house of Rabbi Tamar <note>a reference to the Talmudic passage in Yevamot regarding Tamar's beauty or oil</note>. Why is it called "Tamar oil"? Because it is made like a palm tree (*Tamar*), as mentioned regarding the finger. Now see that she inserts the longest finger into the ring to protect her uniqueness for him. Thus, that "Surrounding Light" of the Betrothal which surrounded the finger remains there until the time of intimacy, when he gives her the Inner Spirit. Then, the "Body of the Betrothal" becomes the secret of the surrounding light for the Inner Spirit.

Because of this secret, one must sanctify the woman on the long finger <note>the middle finger</note> for the reason mentioned above. We also find in the commentary of Rabbeinu Bahya on the portion of *Noach* that natural philosophers wrote that the middle finger alone is used for certain medicinal purposes. The middle finger is also connected to the "cord of nourishment" which extends to all parts of the body; therefore, it is longer than all of them. Thus, the secret of the finger is specifically on the long finger. There is another secret regarding this finger: it represents the "Long Letter" <note>likely the letter Vav or a stretched Nun</note> that descends from the Supernal Crown of the "Ancient of Days" <term>Atik: the highest, most hidden level of the Divine</term>. As mentioned, it is revealed within the long finger, as is known regarding the Throne where the five letters <note>the final forms of Hebrew letters: MNZPK</note> are divided among the fingers; the "Long One" comes to the long finger, which is the *Ammah*. Know that later, on page 130b, it speaks of the "Voice of the Living Spirit" of the Ancient One regarding the "Hidden Brain" <term>Mocha Stima'ah: the concealed wisdom of the Divine</term>.

<column-break/>

...to the appearance of the "Brains" <term>Mohin: divine intellectual energies</term>. The explanation is this: it is known that the light of the Ancient One (*Atik*) is clothed within the Hidden Brain of the "Long Face" <term>Arich Anpin: the macro-prosopus or divine patience</term>, and from there it spreads to the "Female of the Hidden Brain" and descends and spreads into the brain of the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin: the emotional attributes of the Divine</term>, and from there into the majority of the intellects.

Know that the Hidden Brain is called the "Point" <term>Kutza: a small stroke or point on a Hebrew letter</term> which contains the attributes of Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge. The main power of these attributes is at the "Navel of the Long Face." See also in the *Tikunei Zohar*, at the beginning of the fifth Tikun, page 15, regarding the "Hardened Lantern" <term>Botzina de-Kardinuta: a primordial, restrictive divine light</term> from which this "Point" was made, which is like a square seal. As mentioned regarding Tamar, the groom says to the bride: "Behold, you are sanctified to me with this ring," etc.

The "Voice of the Living Spirit" becomes that seventh voice revealed in the fifth finger, emerging from the thinnest, most refined sound. Therefore, one must also sanctify the woman with this finger to return that "Living Essence" (*Chayah*) there, in the secret of returning the Surrounding Light upon her finger. Without this, the holiness would not be complete. Therefore, the Betrothal ring goes around the entire finger. See the wonder in this finger: through it, the "Shell" is separated <note>referring to the separation of spiritual impurity</note>... the finger contains five "Strengths" <term>Gevurot: divine judgments or constraints</term>, each composed of ten, totaling fifty. These five Strengths always come to her as a Surrounding Light to the Inner Spirit. These Strengths are elevated through the "Awakening from Below" <note>human prayer and action</note>, as the Master wrote. Every single day, those below raise new "sparks" <term>Nitzotzot: divine sparks trapped in the material world</term>. This is the purpose of prayers and preparations. Not all "Kings" are equal, for each one elevates according to his appropriate level. Therefore, all of Israel need one another, and one person cannot do what his fellow does. This is a very great principle.

All of this will continue until the Messiah comes, may he arrive soon. For then, the lower Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> will be established and will awaken on her own to rise, without the assistance of the righteous, but only through the light of the Supernal Holiness. These are his words.

If so, it appears that her main essence in the future will be that "Long Letter" mentioned, and her final construction will be through the letter *Zayin*, though now we still require assistance from those below, as mentioned.

# Laws of Tefillin

At the time of exile <note>original: "גולה" (Golah)</note> in the outside world, the "Mental Faculties" <note>term: "Mohin" (Mental Faculties) — In Kabbalah, these represent the higher divine energies or consciousness that descend into the lower spheres.</note> are from our own efforts, and there is no greater flaw than this. And you already know that whenever a person's soul is elevated above its natural level, they are scrutinized even for a minor transgression, relative to the height of the level they reached. Once, the Rabbi <note>Referring to the Ari (Rabbi Isaac Luria), the 16th-century mystic.</note> of blessed memory was in wonderment because he was suspected of a lack of integrity regarding peace <note>original: "גזל שלום" (theft of peace/greeting)</note>. When he wanted to ascend to a great spiritual state, they scrutinized him because once he was focusing his intentions <note>term: "Kavanah" (Intention) — The specific mystical focus or meditation directed during prayer.</note> on the "Sanctification" <note>The Kedushah prayer.</note> and also intended to focus while saying "without understanding" <note>original: "שלא בינה"</note>... <note>The text here contains a parenthetical mystical explanation regarding the birth of souls and the "drops" of spiritual energy, referencing the Bedtime Shema; see there for details.</note>. And if one is born in purity and through the intention that it was the Sabbath, yet his mind was distracted from the Tefillin, they would remove him. Therefore, one must be careful regarding the "Fear of the King."

### When one should remove the Tefillin
### during the Morning Prayer

-> The Rabbi said that one must <-
-> be careful not to remove <-

the Tefillin from his head until after the prayer "It is our duty to praise" <note>original: "Aleinu L'shabeach" — the closing prayer of the service.</note>. Therefore, [wait until] "Hope in the Lord" etc. And when you remove the Tefillin of the hand, it must be done while sitting, just as it was during the writing; and when you remove the Tefillin of the head, remove it while standing, just as it was during the writing. So brings the H.B. <note>likely a reference to a specific Halakhic code</note> in Section 2, Chapter 65 of the Order of Laws. (The R.A.D. wrote that this was found in the Talmudic tractate Menachot, page 35, see there. But when one puts them on, he puts on the hand Tefillin first and then the head; and when he removes them, he removes the head first and then the hand, as it is written: "And they shall be for frontlets between your eyes" — as long as they are between your eyes, both shall be present. This teaches that the head Tefillin are removed while the hand Tefillin are still on. The reason is that after the prayer, when the Mental Faculties depart, they return to the world of the "Essence of the Faculties." First, the essence of the "Outer Faculties" departs, and afterward, the essence of the "Other Faculties" also departs. Because of the "Residue" <note>term: "Reshimo" (Residue) — The spiritual impression or trace left behind after a divine light has departed.</note> that departs from them toward evening, it is the opposite; for when it departs, the residue of the "Feminine" departs, and this is due to the "Ape" <note>A mystical reference to the forces of the "Other Side" or shells of impurity.</note>. But the residue of the "Small Face" <note>term: "Zeir Anpin" (Small Face) — A central Kabbalic persona representing the emotional attributes of God.</note> does not depart until after the Evening Prayer, as mentioned above.)

### The Writing of the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, a prominent 13th-century legalist.</note>

-> As mentioned, there should not be two pairs <-
-> in one bag, for Heaven forbid, it is <-
-> forbidden to put them in the [same] Tefillin bag; rather, one should make two [bags] <-

<column-break/>

on the right and... for each bag, so that one does not touch the other. (The R.G.L. wrote that it is not for this reason that it is forbidden to bring them in one bag because of the sanctity; rather, it is for another reason, as we wrote above in the name of the Ari, of blessed memory, in the laws of the Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam and Rashi <note>note: Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam were medieval scholars who disagreed on the internal order of the parchment scrolls inside Tefillin. Many pious Jews wear both pairs.</note>. See there, for they are two distinct commandments in their appearance and merit. They must be brought in separate vessels because the Tefillin of Rashi are "Holy" and the Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam are "Holy of Holies," because they represent the Mental Faculties of the "Father" <note>term: "Abba" (Father) — The Sephirah of Wisdom (Chokhmah).</note>. And it is known that before the Mental Faculties enter at all, his faculties which cover "Wisdom" are clothed in the vessels of the Father alone, and his faculties which cover "Understanding" are clothed in the vessels of the Mother <note>term: "Imma" (Mother) — The Sephirah of Understanding (Binah).</note> alone. Afterward, they are clothed in the Wisdom/Understanding of the Father within the Wisdom/Understanding of the Mother, and they enter together into the "Small Face" to form the aspect of the Tefillin. Therefore, since before they enter together they are each distinct faculties, one must also have for each pair of Tefillin a bag for itself. And so it is written in the Talmud in the name of Rabbi Isaac of Corbeil. And so the Tur ruled in Section 25. This is the opposite of what was written here by one who suggested putting two pairs in one bag—and may his honor be forgiven, for this is the opposite of the Kabbalah and the legal decisors. The case of the Tefillin is called the "Vessels of the Father" or "Vessels of the Mother." And this is a hint, for the word "Bag" <note>original: "תיק" (Tik)</note> is an acronym for "Two Thighs of Truth" <note>original: "תרין ירכי קשוט" (Trin Yarchei Keshot) — a Zoharic phrase.</note>.) (In which in the morning he is wrapped in a Tallit <note>Prayer shawl.</note> and Tefillin on his head and arm, his intention [is set], and afterward he shall go to the Synagogue thus wrapped, and he must check the Mezuzah.)

# Laws of Tefillin
->The bride is sweetened at the time of the Seven Blessings<-
### And after one has placed the Tefillin of the head, it is good to place the ends of the straps inside
**his belt** <note>Hebrew: *avnet*</note> so that they do not touch the ground, contrary to those who are careful to let them hang to the ground.
<margin>For as mentioned above, the mystery of the "Atarah" (Crown) is as the Rabbi <note>Isaac Luria, the "Ari"</note> explained above: that the right strap, which is the "wing" of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, is the kindness that extends only to the navel of the Small Face <note>Zeir Anpin/the divine persona</note>.</margin>
And the left strap, which is the "wing" of Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, reaches until the navel of the Female <note>Nukva</note>. And this is the secret of the "Sign" <note>the covenant/circumcision</note> that is revealed in the male of Israel through strength. Therefore, it is necessary that its end be tucked into his belt to show that the essence of the straps does not reach further than the belt, which is the location of their "light." However, the "surplus" of the lights extends to the end of the Female, which is the secret of the "Sign" revealed.
### **Furthermore,** the Rabbi <note>of blessed memory</note> wrote that one must meditate on the straps because
the name <term>EL (God)<gloss>spelled Aleph-Lamed</gloss></term> when filled out <note>spelling out the names of the letters</note> equals 185, and likewise the name <term>EL (God)</term> when filled out with the name <term>KOH</term> equals the numerical value of "Master of the Universe" <note>Ribbono Shel Olam</note>, which is the secret of the "Sign" in the belts.

# That one should not divert his mind from the Tefillin all day
### Even during the prayer itself. And this is my personal custom:
It is worthy, either during the Silent Prayer <note>the Amidah</note> or when one is occupied with Torah study—since it is impossible for a person to focus on all the mystical intentions at every single moment, as one must also focus on the meaning of the prayers—therefore, if one focused on the proper intentions at the time of putting on the Tefillin, that is sufficient. But during the rest of the prayer time or the middle of the day, you should focus on the "Short Intention" as follows: namely, that in the Tefillin of the head there are the names **EHYEH, HOVAH, EHYEH** <note>I Will Be, Being, I Will Be</note> in their simple form. And afterward, focus on the Tefillin of the arm on the names **EHYEH, HOVAH, ADONAI** in their simple form. The sum of these names equals 70, the numerical value of "Secret" <note>Sod</note>. Do not let this short intention depart from your eyes at every single moment, even when you are saying the prayers, except during the Standing Prayer or during Torah study alone, as mentioned. And the Rabbi <note>of blessed memory</note> was very strict about this matter, for the matter of "diverting the mind" <column-break/> is like the time of union called "Knowledge" <note>Da'at</note>, which is the union of the "Kindnesses" <note>Chasadim</note> first.
So too, the "Knowledge" which is the "Seven" in the head is also called such at the time of their adornment, and they are the ones who bring the "Rectification" <note>Tikkun</note> as explained by the Zohar. And regarding the secret of the ring: just as she is sanctified with a ring, so too "Blessed is He who sanctifies His people." And he places it on the middle finger of the hand, which is the image of the "Sign" and the "Crown." And "Blessed are the two witnesses" <note>the breasts/supports</note> which are the "Praise of the Bride." And when the ring is on the middle finger, at that time one must bless her with the Seven Blessings through which the Bride is blessed. From here it is understood that since it says "Blessed is He who sanctifies her" on her finger, and the Rabbi <note>of blessed memory</note> explained that the end of the finger is the ring on the finger called the "Middle Finger" <note>Amah</note>, which is the secret of the "Holy of Holies." Therefore, it is proper to also place the "Head" <note>the knot/wrap</note> on the finger called the Middle Finger. And since the sweetness of the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> and the names of the fingers are each called "Yod," therefore through the names of the fingers, she becomes a "Light" that surrounds the "Vessel," which is the secret of the "Seven." And through the names of the "Kindnesses," she is made at that time into an "Inner Vessel" through the Seven Blessings—meaning the "Well of Living Water" that comes out of the "Ring," which is the Foundation. The flow that comes from it is called the "Well of Life," and "My God, my soul is within me." And we wrote above that the letter *Zayin* <note>numerical value 7</note> is revealed in the arm of the Small Face, and afterward when the letter *Yod* <note>10</note> is revealed in the middle finger, or by making the letter *Shin* on the head and making the secret of the name *Shaddai*. And if so, one must bless her with the Seven Blessings to inherit her. That is to say, since she already has the "Surrounding Light," she now needs to be blessed from the Foundation of the Small Face to make her an "Inner Vessel," for "Israel does not make a covenant except with one who makes her a vessel." And these are the Seven Blessings, which are the "Seven" that come out of the Foundation called "Zayin." "Bless Seven, Create Seven" in those "Seven Voices" which are the point of the Foundation. And the root of these Seven Blessings are the seven aspects of Kindnesses—namely, five Kindnesses until Majesty <note>Hod</note> and two "Inclusions" of Foundation and Sovereignty <note>Yesod and Malchut</note>, totaling seven. And likewise, seven aspects of "Strengths" <note>Gevurot</note>. And the Kindnesses themselves are 500 Kindnesses and 500 Strengths, each included in the other, totaling 1000. This is the hint: "The thousand is for you, Solomon." And this is the hint that the words of the Seven Blessings contain three "Alephs," which are the "Thousand Blessings."

# Laws of the Mezuzah

In those places, protection is required. And for what reason, then, do we place [the Mezuzah] on the upper doorpost, which is a "good place"—a place that does not strictly require protection? Yet in the place that *does* require protection, they do not place Mezuzahs? Behold, further on, these matters are cited in the name of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of contemporary Kabbalah</note>, and as a scholar, they are hidden from me. If so, how is it possible that the *Malchut* pushes away the writing of the Mezuzah portions? According to this, it would be appropriate to place the Mezuzah specifically on the door of the house and not on the doorposts at all. And how is the third Mezuzah related to the "contributions" for *Malchut*? Furthermore, I also found other matters in the name of the Ari, of blessed memory, regarding the aspect of the Mezuzah, and because the words are so strange that I have not tasted their good flavor—not even a mere spirit of understanding is there—therefore I did not copy them, except for the first. May God enlighten my eyes with the light of His Torah and lead me in the path of truth so that I do not stumble.

# Laws of the Mezuzah

->**The Reception of Lights**<-

And behold, the reception of the lights from the *Yesod* <note>The sefirah of Foundation, representing the generative organ</note> is revealed, and therefore it is in a state of greater sweetness. However, within the "Rachel of Rachel" <note>A specific sub-level of the divine persona Rachel</note> there are eight pairs of blessing. For initially, there were the partitions of the wall of Rachel which was close and attached to Leah. Afterward, there are the two partitions of the legs of Leah. Each leg contains three partitions and three walls, and afterward, there is another inner partition of Rachel, and over all of them is the Face—meaning there are many levels of partitions and walls there. Therefore, the lights that reach the *Keter* <note>Crown</note> of Rachel cannot pass through to the Face to illuminate it through so many partitions. In the partition that separates Rachel, there are also five courtyards, just as in Leah.

And behold, besides this, there in the legs of Leah is the stronghold of the "External Ones" <note>The *Chitzonim* or demonic forces</note>. And Balaam <note>The biblical sorcerer, here representing a cosmic force of evil</note> swallowed those lights, preventing them from emerging in the place where they are swallowed, in the *Keter* of Rachel. 

And behold, <term>Balaam</term> <note>The name is broken down here as an acronym or mystical cipher</note> represents the six [lights] of the five [severities]... which are the lights of Leah and Rachel that they take from the *Zeir Anpin* <note>The "Small Face" or masculine divine persona</note>. Balaam and Balak take them, as the verse says: *And he shall remove his sin, his law* <note>A mystical reading of a biblical fragment</note>. The intention is that, as mentioned, Balaam was in the place of the "tail" of the *Yesod* of *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>, called *Shelez* <note>Numerical value 337</note>, and his form is like the image of the "Other Side" <note>The *Sitra Achra* or evil realm</note> on the outside. It is that same *Shelez*, only that his "law" extends into the *Keter* of *Zeir Anpin*. And his escape is below, where he takes hold of Rachel... and also *he removed his sin, my law*—this is the secret of *Shelez* itself, only his partition is there... Therefore, the "disturber" Balaam is the illumination of the *Yesod* of *Abba* <note>The Father/Wisdom persona</note> which extends to this place. 

However, Balak is from the descendants of Jethro. This is "Balak son of Zippor," for *Zippor* <note>Bird</note> refers to Jethro, in the secret of *Even a bird finds a home* as mentioned in the Zohar, page 136. And behold, Jethro comes from Cain, a rectification for *Binah*. Thus, Balak is the secret of the legs themselves of Leah, and he is called "Son of 72" <note>The Name of 72 letters</note> who ages and breaks through those legs into the *Keter* of Rachel. This is what is written, "Balak son of Zippor," who emerges from there to the outside, to the External Ones. This is called Balak, and he is scattered into four words of the Names *Av, Sag, Mah, and Ban* <note>The four primary expansions of the Tetragrammaton</note> with their four collective sums, which are the illumination of the "Brains" of the partitions in Leah... as is known, for the disturber is the L[amed]... and likewise Uzza and Azael <note>Fallen angels</note> are thorns in the heels of

Leah that enter into Rachel-Leah. And behold, "to die" with the [letter] *He*... and the reason is that the letter *He* in the three fillings... to say that Uzza and Azael, the creation is handed over from between the legs of Leah to Rachel. Rachel [receives] from the right leg where the light is stronger and they are not so easily damaged by them. > <margin>In the foreign tongue <note>original: "Be-la'az"</note> it is handed down to this firstborn from the *Yalkut* on Portion Bereshit: that Shamchazai and Azael are angels who fell from heaven etc. Behold, Shamchazai repented, but Azael did not repent etc. And the explanation is that Azael took the letter *Vav* and... and became Azael to indicate the change. The matter is that since during the creation of *Adam Kadmon* <note>The Primordial Man</note> it was known that initially <term>ZON</term> <note>Zeir Anpin and Nukva; the masculine and feminine aspects</note> were "back-to-back," and in the expansion to create Leah they needed to be "face-to-face." And behold, they were not yet turned face-to-face. That portion of Uzza and Azael was there, for the heels of Leah were inside Rachel only while she was back-to-back. But when Rachel turns face-to-face, the heels of Leah are no longer inside her. And all the "seals" of the lights that they were suckling from the back, from the *Keter* of Rachel—from which the angels Uzza and Azael took their sustenance—when she was revealed, that part left. For all the lights are now drawn to the Face, because that is where Rachel stands. Therefore, Uzza and Azael tried to prevent the creation of *Adam Kadmon* so that they would not turn face-to-face, so that their life-force would not be nullified. 

And thus, Balaam... to strengthen Uzza and Azael.

### But

->The forms of the Living Creatures are imprinted<-
->in the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the secret imprint<-
->of the Mezuzah:<- The name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> is from the outside, and the name *YHVH* is from the inside.
And the secret of the imprint of the Covenant of Circumcision <term>Brit Milah</term> is that *Shaddai* is from the outside and *YHVH* is from the inside. Regarding *Shaddai*, the sages established that the letter **Shin** (ש) represents three "faces" <note>original: *anpin*</note> of love: the two arms and the body. These are the three faces. The **Dalet** (ד) is the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>. The **Yod** (י) is the sign of the Covenant of Circumcision. Regarding this, it is said: "And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty (*El Shaddai*)" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. In the aspect of *Shaddai*, it is compressed from the outside like a Mezuzah, but "My name *YHVH*" is compressed from the inside like a Mezuzah. This is the "Gate of the Lord" of which it is said: "This is the gate to the Lord" <note>Psalm 118:20</note>, "I was not known to them." "And you shall write them upon the doorposts (*mezuzot*) of your house and upon your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 6:9</note>—these are the two "Supports of Truth" <term>the sefirot Netzach and Hod</term>. "Moving away from the house" refers to the *Shekhinah*... and the secret of "the stranger who approaches shall be put to death" <note>Numbers 1:51</note>. The letters of the word *Mezuzot* (מזוזת) are literally "Moving Death" (*Zaz Mavet*). Therefore, one who writes the Covenant of Circumcision, which is His seal, "Death moves" away from him. Thus far his words.

And it appears to me, Nathan, that despite the aforementioned introductions, this discourse will be understood on its own. Even though this clothes the "Back" of the Long Face, the primary rectification is from the Father of the Long Face, for there is the spreading of the Kindnesses... and so the two females, Rachel and Leah, even though they clothe all the "Backs" of the Father and the Long Face, their primary rectification is from the "Foundation of the Long Face," for there the Severities of the Long Face are revealed from the "Hidden Brain" as is known. Therefore, the **Zohar** and the **Tikunim** said: "He is in the 'Back' and She is in the 'Light'." The Foundation of the Mother, which is revealed outwardly... is the secret of these intentions as will be explained later.

## One must place the Mezuzah on the right side of the entrance.
## And it is the right side relative to entry, not the
## right side relative to exit.

> (And the secret is as written in the Talmud, Tractate Menachot, chapter *HaKometz*, page 34):
> It was taught in a Baraita: "And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house"—this means the way you enter, on the right. You say on the right; but perhaps it is only on the left? The Torah says "your house" (*beitekha*). What is the derivation? Rabba said: It is the way you enter, for when a person moves his legs, he moves the right one first.

The explanation is as follows: "Your entry" is the way of your walking. Since the language of "entry" was used, it implies we require the right side of entry and not the right side of exit. The secret of this is that the Mezuzah is written from the "Back" of the Small Face, which is the clothing for the "Legs" of the Mother, which are the aspect of "the doorposts of your house"—the two "Supports of Truth." There, the "Splendor" <term>Hod</term> of the Mother is fully revealed. This is what is meant by "And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house"—meaning the writing in the Mezuzah is by the power of the right-side walking of the doorposts of the Long Face, the two "Thighs of Truth" in glory. And this resolved the difficulty for the sages regarding the curtain...

# Laws of the Mezuzah

Specifically to place it in the upper third, as I have written simply in my previous comments <note>original: "נדמ"ש" - likely referring to the author's own glosses or a specific commentary</note>, neither lower nor higher; for we have not written this for no reason, as the Sages were able to speak according to their words.

## The Commandment to Place it Within the Hollow of the Entrance

->(And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said there, and these are their words: )<-

**Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel: It is a commandment to place it within the hollow of the entrance.**

The intention is as he said: that initially, the influence should spread literally within the hollow, from the inside to the outside of the *Zeir* <note>Zeir Anpin: the "Small Face" or emotional attributes in Kabbalah</note>, and from there it is revealed outside to the "back" where the "External Forces" <note>the *Chitzonim* or spiritual husks</note> draw their nourishment, which is called the "Public Domain." Thus, one must place the Mezuzah within the hollow of the entrance as well, so as not to allow the connection of *Binah* <note>Understanding/Divine Mother</note> to lean more toward the back of the *Zeir* by way of the "Passages" <note>original: "פסי"ס" - likely referring to spiritual conduits</note>. This is so that the External Forces, who suckle there at the back of the *Zeir*, do not have a place to take from. Therefore, he said:

**Rava said: It is a commandment to place it within the handbreadth (*Tefach*) adjacent to the Public Domain. What is the reason? The Rabbis say: So that one encounters the commandment immediately.**

This means to say: since the *Nukva* <note>the Feminine principle/Malchut</note> receives all her influence from the *Yesod* <note>Foundation</note> of *Zeir* which is revealed on the outside, therefore the work of the Higher Artisan <note>the Creator/Divine system</note> is that the *Yesod* of *Binah* should rise in the handbreadth adjacent to the outside of *Zeir*, which is called the "Private Domain" <note>original: "רה"י"</note>, for the interior of *Zeir* is called the Private Domain of the world. And the back of *Zeir* is the back of the External Forces. It must be in the handbreadth adjacent to the Public Domain <note>original: "רה"ר"</note> because the *Malchut* <note>Kingship</note> stands there, so that they can receive our influence immediately without delay.

**And Rav Huna said: So that it may guard him.**

This means to say: the Higher Work was not done for the sake of *Malchut* alone, but rather for the sake of the External Forces who suckle there from the *Nukva*. Therefore, the *Yesod* of *Binah*—which is the aspect of the Mezuzah—must be revealed there to drive away all the External Forces by means of the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty - traditionally written on the back of the Mezuzah</note>, which terrifies all the "shells" (*Klipot*). And this is the meaning of "so that it may guard him"—to guard the entire house from the "Damagers" <note>spiritual pests or demons</note>.

**And now**, according to the words of the Teacher of the *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei Zohar</note> page 84, until here. And these are the words: (For all the sparks are equal, they are hidden in the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, like the mark of the Mezuzah, to be a healing for the door from the outside, the Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note> from the outside).

<column-break/>

It is written on the outside <note>referring to the Divine Name on the scroll</note>. For others, "my right hand" <note>original: "ימיני"</note> is the numerical value of 112 <note>the name Yabok</note>, a sign of the "curtain" <note>original: "פרס"א"</note> of charities. And this is the intention of what is called "Suseyah" <note>a mystical name for the Mezuzah</note>, an angel. And "my right hand" is the power to indicate the *Yesod* (Foundation). For example, within the *Yesod* there is a power to attain the "Gevurah" (Strength) and "Gedulah" (Greatness) of *Binah*... and it is the secret of "from His right hand" <note>Deuteronomy 33:2</note>. This is understood to mean that in the place where the *Yesod* of *Binah* is added—which is called "His right hand"—there the *Nukva* begins to be built... which is called "Benjamin" <note>literally 'Son of the Right'</note>. For until that point, the influence of *Binah* reaches, because it is always called "Right," and its opposite is called "Left." And behold, since the lower *Yesod* is the secret of the Mezuzah, and it ends with the secret of the "Covenant" <note>circumcision/foundation</note>... therefore the Mezuzah is placed according to the verse that requires placing the Mezuzah on the right, and not on the left. For the secret descends below to the secret of the "Ten," and it has no connection with the Mezuzah at all... and this is why one must go to the right upon entry, to show that at the time of entering and looking toward God... the aspect of the Mezuzah is revealed. But if one went to the left upon entry, then the aspect of the Mezuzah would be withdrawn, and that is the time of the withdrawal of the "Mochin" <note>Divine Intellects</note>. The Sages requested to draw the *Mochin* always into the essence... within the Mezuzah, which is the "Right" of standing up. Therefore, one must place the Mezuzah on the right side of the entry. And this is correct.

Therefore, one must measure a third from the lintel down the height of the entrance, and at the end of that third, he shall place the Mezuzah—neither less nor more. This is not like what some of the legal decisors <note>Halakhic authorities</note> wrote, that one can place it at the height of the entrance on the lintel itself. That is the opposite of the [mystical] intention, for the aspect of the Mezuzah is not revealed on the top of the *Zeir*... rather, the aspect of the Mezuzah ends there and does not spread higher.
